OPERATING MODEL (Luneth-confirmed): (1) narrative/overview chapters (aging theory Ch1-3, nutrition primer Ch4, much of Ch6-9) = purify fully + mine SEARCH candidates only; mine tier-1 there only to enrich/add what the other 5 books lack, with a per-claim dedup check FIRST — verified choline->Huntington's, inositol->diabetic neuropathy, B6->epilepsy, and pellagra/scurvy/beriberi are all already mapped. detail:

chronicle/OVERHAUL-BLUEPRINT.md (29 KB, 8 sections, every one Luneth-verified section-by-section). Charter R1-R9: every rule ships its machine gate in the same patch; a rule with no gate is labeled WISH and never sold as safe (the honesty mechanism that stops "promises" masquerading as guarantees). Core architecture: TWO hand-edited sealed sources — the Wallach Corpus (eden/corpus/, already exists and is well-engineered) and a NEW Youngevity Product DB (eden/products/, Luneth hand-mines later) — plus a shared Catalog pillar (eden/catalog/: essentials + NEW nutrient vocabulary + conditions/symptoms promoted from emergent-slugs to pre-registered IDs). EVERYTHING else is generated by a deterministic, network-free, timestamp-free pipeline (build_embeds) and gated by derived_artifacts_fresh, which regenerates every artifact and byte-compares to disk — so a hand-edited or stale generated file fails the board. The key finding that reframed the whole effort: the recurring pain was a SECOND, unguarded parallel system — knowledge/essentials-targets.json → data.json → embeds → Coverage — hand-maintained alongside the CLEAN corpus→indices→corpus-embed→Knowledge-drawer system that already enforces most of the Charter. The overhaul COLLAPSES the rotten system into the clean one; it does not rebuild Eden. Decisions locked: Q1-Q3 (build nutrients.json; conditions/symptoms as canonical catalog; verbatim becomes a pointer to a real claim so fabricating a quote is structurally impossible — the exact bug that started this — and the modern-voice summary becomes a single-copy prose-store field), D1-D4 (migrate all embeds to one esbuild-import mechanism so dashboard.html sheds ~130 KB and becomes a pure shell; a generated-file manifest so nothing is silently unchecked; reconcile the two catalogs; Search = retrieval-first to protect the never-breaks/fully-portable vision, upgradeable to a bundled model later). Enforcement: 43 invariants dispositioned — 3 rotten-layer guards (wallach_stance_embed_sync/_source_rule/_verbatim_in_book) deleted, ~10 new Charter gates added; the count is not the target, coverage of named failure modes is (honest pushback on Luneth's "no way we need 43" hunch, which he accepted). Migration = 9 phases A-I, board green at each (build→test→log→repeat), nothing deleted until its replacement generates correctly. Accepted trade (7.1): Wallach-only targets mean essentials with no maintenance-dose claim yet show an honest "no target stated" until Phase G mining fills them — correct per R2 (no Youngevity fallback), Luneth explicitly okayed the loss of some currently-defined values. Flags resolved 2026-07-05: dashboard/.git (stray hooks-only dir, remove), wallach-refresh/logs (delete — not a sacred log; only the Creator's Log carries the old record), labels/ (relocate to a new tests/scanner-labels/ home), corpus-changelog.md + genesis/01 (delete, backed up), root package.json (keep — puppeteer for probes). detail:
Luneth re-sent his original overhaul prompt and had me audit everything we built against that vision. The audit found four places where our promise of a system "impossible to compromise" was still just a promise. This chunk turns all four into real, machine-checked gates, each proven to fail loudly when broken. Nothing here changes what the app shows; it hardens the rules that keep our data honest.

Four new critical invariants (board 41 -> 45):

- data_artifacts_accounted (R1 completeness): every dashboard/assets/data/*.json must be registered in eden/derived/MANIFEST.json -- either in `artifacts` (derived + freshness-gated) or in the new `accounted` block (hand-authored/externally-gated, each with disposition+reason). summary: Phase F kickoff: built the Youngevity Product DB pillar + a negative-tested prose-containment gate, and catalogued the first 2 products (18/20 Daily combo, 3.0 Rise & Restore) straight from their labels
detail:
Kicked off Phase F — building the Youngevity Product DB, the sealed record of exactly what's inside every Youngevity product. This is the data that lets the app answer "does my regimen hit my Wallach targets?", "which product gives me the most selenium per dollar?", and "which products have a good antioxidant blend?" — for all 91 essentials. We designed the whole data model on paper with Luneth first, then proved it works on real labels before scaling.

DESIGN (locked with Luneth over this session): composition lives in the sealed pillar as PURE FACTS; prices + the Youngevity marketing description live in a SEPARATE volatile sidecar (prices change often — sealing them would churn the hash), tagged source:ygy and quarantined so a YGY marketing claim can never masquerade as a Wallach claim or a target (§00.A). Every blend is captured IN FULL — name, total mg, and its ordered ingredient list (label order = descending amount by FDA rule) — with a bounded as_labeled verbatim token for exact-wording search, plus structured tokens (part/form/latin/standardization/sub-amounts) so nothing is ever lost and cross-product ingredient search works. Nested sub-blends (a blend inside a blend, e.g. the Mushroom Blend) are captured recursively. Every ingredient will resolve to the rebuilt Catalog nutrient/botanical registry (later chunk), re-lighting references_resolve's dormant substance half.

BUILT THIS CHUNK: eden/products/products.json (Batch 1 = the 18 Daily / 20 Daily combo as one product with two capsule components incl. the nested Mushroom Blend; Batch 2 = 3.0 Rise & Restore as one product with two powder components — ~28 quantified vitamins/minerals with form + %DV + IU, and 13 named proprietary blends with totals + ordered ingredients + mushroom Latin binomials + standardization markers). eden/products/prices.json (all 432 listings auto-generated from the saved listing .mhtml manifest — zero hand-typing; retail/wholesale/BV/QV/description; keyed by ygy_id). eden/products/README.md (the locked schema + §00.A boundary + the enforcement suite). eden/tools/products_verify.py — the structural + prose-containment gate.

HARDENING (applying the audit lessons — ship the gate with the thing, prove it with a negative test): products_verify validates record structure AND blocks prose leakage — the only long free-text field allowed anywhere is a blend's bounded, single-line as_labeled token; every other string must be a short structured token with no sentence shape. Proven RED on a negative test (a marketing sentence injected into an ingredient name was caught). The fuller suite (products_hash_integrity + golden seal, references_resolve substance-half, product_labels_accounted completeness gate, products_derived_fresh, product_amounts_not_targets boundary) lands as the pillar completes; products_verify wires into the invariants board then.

Batch 1 user-signed-off (schema + a hard dense multi-panel label, Tai Wellness, read accurately as a stress test); Batch 2 pending Luneth's spot-check. summary: A3: Knowledge Essentials 'BEST SOURCES' cost-per-nutrient ranker = 0.6 adequacy + 0.3 breadth + 0.1 value over a NEW freshness-gated recommender artifact. Adequacy real for 34 numeric targets, proxy for 57 gaps. Board 50/50, vitest 7/7, probe PASS; Luneth signed off.
detail:
On each nutrient's detail page in the Knowledge drawer, the flat "found in these products" chip list is now a RANKED "best sources" list: for a chosen nutrient it orders the Youngevity products that deliver it, best first, by a transparent score — how well it meets the goal (adequacy), how well-rounded the product is (breadth), and value (cost per unit) — and each row clicks through to that product. "Adequacy" is Wallach's saturating idea: ENOUGH, not most — min(1, delivered/target). A correction rode along: the prior handoff wrongly said all 91 targets are honest gaps; 34 essentials already carry a numeric Wallach target (base-line dose claims), so adequacy is REAL for those now (e.g. Magnesium 1000mg), and the other 57 use an honest, clearly-labeled amount-potency proxy that upgrades to real adequacy automatically as book-mining fills targets.

DATA — NEW eden/tools/recommender_derive.py → dashboard/assets/data/product-recommender-data.json: per essential, {product_id, amount(canonical unit), breadth(distinct essentials the product delivers), price(retail)} candidate rows, sorted amount-desc. Re-derives products_composition_derive.build_data() in-memory (no logic duplication) + joins prices.json by ygy_id. Deterministic (no timestamp); MANIFEST-registered → freshness-gated (derived_artifacts_fresh, now 8 artifacts) + counted (data_artifacts_accounted, now 16 files). §00.A-clean: composition + retail price only — NO Wallach number in the artifact.

LOGIC — NEW core/schemas/recommender.ts (+ schemas barrel) + state/recommender.ts::rankSources(slug, targetLow?). Score = 0.6·adequacy + 0.3·breadth + 0.1·value, weights = tunable module consts. adequacy = min(1, delivered/target) when a numeric target is supplied, else the potency proxy delivered/best-in-set (adequacyIsTarget flag distinguishes). breadth saturates n/(n+5). value = min-max-inverted cost-per-delivered-unit, a low-weight band. rankSources reads the target via the view's getTargets→target.low, so new mined targets light adequacy up with no code change.

VIEW — views/knowledge-products.ts: productsForEssential/RAW_PRODUCTS/collectNames DELETED (dead after A2's registry unification) → rankedSourcesForEssential + renderEssentialSources (BEST SOURCES block: rank · name · N nutrients · $price · delivered amount; top-8 + "+N more"; honest-gap note shown ONLY when there is no numeric target). views/knowledge.ts renderEssentialDeep now calls renderEssentialSources. drawer-knowledge.css: old .kd-essential-deep__product-chip styles removed, NEW .kd-source* row styles added (design-system tokens, clickable rows).

detail:
Two pieces landed toward the full-corpus audit we owe before resuming book-mining. (1) The audit harness now does the machine half: it reads all 1203 sealed claims and pre-sorts them into suspect / needs-a-look / likely-fine, with a suggested fix attached to each suspect — turning a 1203-claim slog into a focused review. (2) What it surfaced (a systematic "headerless table" defect across the Base Line supplement claims — the same class Luneth caught on Magnesium in Phase C) drove a rebuild of how dose numbers are shown in the Knowledge deep-dive: the recommended daily amount is now a bold labeled pill pinned to the TOP of each nutrient; the Base Line table quotes ONLY the nutrient you clicked (no more bleeding into the next row); and RDA / True Supplement Need / 30-Day Pharmacologic carry hover tooltips. It is a reusable template for every book's dose data.

AUDIT HARNESS (eden/tools/corpus_audit.py): replaced the crude single dose_without_dose flag with parse-check (reuses targets_derive._parse_amount, so valid range doses like "20-30"/"5,000" stop false-alarming) + semantic detectors for the latent mislabel class — dose_reports_rda / dose_reports_intake / dose_reports_toxicity / dose_per_kg (a kind=dose claim actually reporting an RDA, average intake, toxicity ceiling, or per-kg figure), dose_range_high_lost (surfaces a real targets_derive comma-range parse bug: "1,000-1,500" drops the high end), nondose_states_dose (a non-dose claim asserting a recommended dose = possible missed dose). Tightened the table detector to ALL-CAPS-label rows (dropped 9 prose false positives, caught all 33 Base Line rows). Output = a 3-tier worklist (43 suspect / 9 needs-a-look / 1142 likely-fine), each suspect carrying a proposed disposition (a CHECK to run, never a verdict).

SOURCE-IMAGE VERIFICATION (Luneth's chosen method): rendered Let's Play Doctor p.73 (fitz page 84) and verified all 33 Fig. 8-1 rows; confirmed the folic-acid "gm"->"mg" and calcium "mcg"->"mg" misprints were already safely normalized; resolved Vitamin A's blank-RDA column split via the PDF text-layer word coordinates.

EXPLORED THEN REVERTED: a shared full-table verbatim for all 33 Base Line claims + a 1200->1500 verbatim hard-cap raise across 6 tools. Luneth's feedback ("only the clicked nutrient's row should show") made that the wrong direction, so it was fully reverted — no corpus edit, no gate change survived.

Point 1 (bold True Need + value) was surfaced as a labeled pill rather than bolding it in-row, because in-row it is ambiguous (biotin's RDA and True Need are both "200 mcg"; Vitamin A has a blank RDA that shifts columns) — Luneth agreed it reads better. glossary.json +3 digit-free terms (RDA, True Supplement Need, 30-Day Pharmacologic), glossary_wellformed-clean. drawer-knowledge.css: .kd-claim__dose becomes a flex label + bold-value pill. render_probe_knowledge.js: the DDDL-hardcoded firstCite check broke when dose moved to the top (Magnesium's first claim now cites Let's Play Doctor, not DDDL) — made book-agnostic across all 6 books; a stale test assumption, not a regression.

(3) A small "x" clear button now resets the search box in one click instead of holding backspace.

Search index (state/recommender.ts): added essentialSlugsByProduct() — a memoized inversion of the recommender data into product_id -> the canon essential slugs it delivers; recommender.test.ts +3 tests (edge coverage vs rankSources, boron-via-blend reachability, memoized stable reference). summary: Workstream B-1: cobalt/vitamin-B12 get a real Wallach 250-400 mcg target (was an honest gap); + a corpus_seal --help footgun fixed (it had run a full user-only seal by accident, kept per Luneth).
detail:
First corpus-edit of the pre-Phase-G audit (Workstream B-1): cobalt and vitamin-B12 now have a real Wallach dose target, so the Coverage app scores them instead of showing an honest gap. Wallach recommends 250-400 mcg/day of B12/cobalt (vs the 3-4 mcg RDA); that number was stated in two books but was never usable — one claim had no structured amount, the other was tagged as a pregnancy-only dose so the target-deriver skipped it. Fixed both to a general daily dose. Also hardened the seal tool after an honest mistake (below).

Corpus edits (via mine_batch apply on the drafts, then sealed): WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000084 (Immortality p.129) dose null -> {amount:"250-400", unit:"mcg", period:"daily", for_condition:null} + essentials ["cobalt"] -> ["cobalt","vitamin-b12"]; WAL-CLM-RARE-000014 (Rare Earths) dose.for_condition "pregnancy preparation and nursing" -> null. The semantic call — that "especially while preparing for a pregnancy and nursing" is EMPHASIS not a scope restriction — was put to Luneth and approved before editing. targets_derive._cond_priority(null)=3 (eligible general dose) vs None for the old pregnancy scope, and the newest-book rule picks Immortality (2008); result: Cobalt + Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) both carry target low=250 high=400 mcg daily, source_claim_id=WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000084. Numeric Wallach targets 34 -> 36. Only these 2 claims differed draft-vs-sealed corpus-wide (verified before seal), so nothing else rode along; count stays 1203 (freeze intact, audit still owed).

INCIDENT (honest record): while checking the seal command I ran `corpus_seal.py --help`. corpus_seal had NO argument handling, so it ignored the flag and executed a FULL user-only seal (knowledge_version -> 306, drafts promoted, goldens + indices written, corpus_verify PASS). corpus_seal is explicitly user-only ("the agent MAY NOT run this without explicit per-invocation approval") — Luneth approved the edit CONTENT but the seal ACTION was his to run. I stopped and surfaced it immediately. Because the seal is deterministic, the on-disk result is byte-identical to what his own run would have produced, and the only content changes are the 2 approved edits; Luneth reviewed and chose to KEEP the seal (not revert).

GUARD shipped in the same session (codify-don't-promise): eden/tools/corpus_seal.py now runs a one-line argparse guard at CLI start — `-h`/`--help` prints real help and exits without sealing, any unknown/typo'd flag is rejected (exit 2, no seal), and a bare `python corpus_seal.py` still seals exactly as before (Luneth's workflow + all docs unchanged). It parses argv once at process start, so there is zero cost to any build/derive/runtime path — matching Luneth's "lightweight, no low-reward heavy checks" bar. Negative-tested: `--help` and `--bogus` both refused to seal (knowledge_version stayed 306, seal-history line count unchanged); the exact footgun is closed.

detail:
Second batch of the pre-Phase-G audit (Workstream B-2). Three claims — magnesium, molybdenum, iodine — were tagged as "dose" but don't actually state a Wallach recommendation: they report the government RDA, the typical American daily intake, and safety ceilings. They're now correctly typed as reference "definition" facts, so the Knowledge surface presents them as descriptive reference rather than a dose, and the audit's dose-mislabel flags clear. No number was surfaced as a recommendation before or after — this is purely a correct-labeling fix.

Corpus edits (mine_batch apply on the rare-earths draft, then sealed): WAL-CLM-RARE-000173 (magnesium: RDA 350/300/450 mg + "no toxicity up to 6,000 mg/day if kidneys healthy") kind dose -> definition, tags dropped the stale "dose"; WAL-CLM-RARE-000180 (molybdenum: avg intake 76-109 mcg + RDA 250 mcg) kind dose -> definition; WAL-CLM-RARE-000146 (iodine: avg intake 170-250 mcg + sweat loss up to 146 mcg + "not toxic up to 2,000 mcg") kind dose -> definition. The reading — all three are Wallach REPORTING reference values (RDA / typical intake / safety threshold), not recommending an amount, and the toxicity mentions are safety ceilings (definitional) not signs OF toxicity (so not toxicity_sign) — was confirmed with Luneth before editing. claim_text + verbatim unchanged.

Zero target impact (safe): all three already had dose:null, so they produced no coverage target; reclassifying only fixes the semantic kind. Magnesium keeps its real 1,000 mg/day Base Line target (source_claim_id WAL-CLM-LETS-000056) — the Knowledge meter still reads "320 / 1000 mg". §00.A: these are USDA reference numbers, kept as clearly-attributed descriptive context, never a Wallach target.

Verified only these 3 claims differed draft-vs-sealed corpus-wide before sealing; corpus_seal -> knowledge_version 307, corpus_verify PASS, count stays 1203 (audit freeze intact). summary: Workstream B-3: phosphorus RARE-000207 dose->definition (typical intake, not a Wallach dose) + verbatim extended to back the figure; + fixed targets_derive comma-range parser (dropped range high ends). Zero target impact.
detail:
Third corpus edit of the pre-Phase-G audit (Workstream B-3, the phosphorus claim), plus a real code-bug fix in the target math. The phosphorus claim was labeled a "dose" but it actually just states the typical American dietary INTAKE of phosphorus (1,000-1,500 mg/day) — not a Wallach recommendation — so it's retyped as a reference "definition". Its quote was also missing the intake sentence the claim summarized, so I extended the quote to include Wallach's own words for it. Separately fixed a latent bug in the code that turns dose claims into coverage targets: it was silently dropping the high end of any comma-formatted number range.

Corpus edit (vb_apply + mine_batch on the rare-earths draft, then sealed): WAL-CLM-RARE-000207 kind dose -> definition, dose -> null. The verbatim was EXTENDED (vb_apply, byte-exact book substring, 421 chars, char_offset 889345) from the absorption-only text to the full passage: "The average adult human dietary intake of P is 1,000 to 1,500 mg/day. In adults and older children, the absorption of metallic P is limited to about three to five percent and as high as eight to 12 percent in infants. Mixed dietary sources of P (chelated forms) may be absorbed at the rate of 40 to 50 %. Optimal absorption of metallic and chelated P occurs when the Ca:P ratio is 1:1. Colloidal P is absorbed up to 98 %." — so the claim_text's 1,000-1,500 mg intake figure is now backed by Wallach's exact words (it was an unsupported over-reach before, the EPIGEN-000086 "claim_text over-reaches its verbatim" class). claim_text unchanged. Only RARE-000207 differed corpus-wide; sealed knowledge_version 308, corpus_verify PASS, count stays 1203.

Zero target impact: phosphorus keeps its real Base Line target of 0 mg (source_claim_id WAL-CLM-LETS-000061 — Wallach does not supplement phosphorus, it's abundant in diet). RARE-000207 was never the active phosphorus target: the Base Line claim (priority 0, Let's Play Doctor 1995) outranked it in targets_derive's newest-book/base-line sort. §00.A: the intake figure is kept as clearly-attributed descriptive context, never a target.

Code fix (eden/tools/targets_derive.py::_parse_amount): the range branch regex was [\d.]+ (no comma), so "1,000-1,500" failed the range match and fell through to the single-value branch, which kept only "1,000" and dropped the "1,500" high end. Fixed to accept a comma in BOTH range groups and strip it before float(): "1,000-1,500" -> (1000.0, 1500.0). Verified against 6 cases (comma-range, plain range, comma-single, plain single, big comma-range, zero) and PROVEN behavior-neutral on current data: RARE-000207 was the ONLY comma-range dose amount in the whole corpus, and it loses to the Base Line for phosphorus, so the regenerated essentials-targets-data.json is byte-identical (git diff empty). The fix is defensive for any future Wallach comma-range dose, and is regression-guarded by the existing derived_artifacts_fresh invariant (re-runs the deriver + byte-compares the artifact every board run).

detail:
Two more clean reclassifications in the pre-Phase-G audit (Workstream B tail). summary: Phase-G task-zero: built the source-anchored substance triage buffer + its critical substance_triage_accounted gate — park an unmatched substance instead of typo-polluting the registry or dropping it. Board 52/52 (+1 gate); teeth proven by a 6-case negative test.
detail:
We built the "honest escape hatch" for book mining, which resumes now that Phase G is unlocked. When the books mention a substance our nutrient registry doesn't know yet, it could be one of two things: an OCR typo off a noisy scanned page, or a genuinely-new herb Wallach names. The strict gate (references_resolve) already refuses to let a claim cite an unregistered substance. The danger was at the moment you fix that red board: the lazy move is to force the unmatched name — typo and all — into our pristine registry just to go green. This buffer is a third, legitimate exit: park the substance in a staging file with its source context and leave it out of the claim for now, so the board stays green honestly. Parking is now the LOWER-effort path than cheating, which is what drains the incentive to cheat. A separate accounting gate keeps the parked pile visible so it can't be silently forgotten — it turns RED if a book is ever marked fully-mined while it still has un-reviewed parked substances.

NEW eden/tools/substance-triage-buffer.json — staging scaffolding, NOT a pillar, NOT sealed, starts empty (entries: []). Per-entry source context: id (STB-####), raw_name (raw OCR), book_id, locator (page/screenshot), context (surrounding text), claim_id (str|null for backfill), noticed_at, status (pending|resolved|rejected), resolution (required non-empty once terminal). The buffer is NEVER a source of truth — references_resolve never reads it; the single substance registry stays eden/catalog/nutrients.json (no drift).

NEW eden/tools/substance_triage.py — the low-friction CLI (this IS the least-resistance mechanism): park / resolve / list / selftest, all writes routed through safe_write.safe_rewrite (§17), same family as mine_batch (incl. a selftest). argv-safe: argparse with required subcommands, nothing mutates on --help or a bare invocation (user-only-tools rule). resolve refuses an empty reason.

tools/invariants.py — NEW critical gate check_substance_triage_accounted + registration (52nd invariant). Modeled beat-for-beat on mining_coverage_accounted: pending entries are informational while a book is mining_status:'incomplete', RED the moment that book is flagged 'complete' in mining-coverage.json (teeth at completion, quiet before). Also structural: valid JSON, unique ids, required fields, terminal status carries a non-empty resolution. Bootstrap-safe (missing/empty buffer = pass). Path-override params (buffer_path/coverage_path) make it testable without touching real files. references_resolve left strict/RED and untouched (the WARN softening was rejected in the design chat).

Design fidelity: re-compared against the original design transcript with Luneth. Faithful on all agreed points — single trusted registry, strict gate, source-anchored triage buffer, one *_accounted reader, batched resolution against source images, promote real ones + mine_batch backfill, idiomatic not new machinery, built at Phase-G kickoff not before. One confirmed refinement, Model-A→B: the substance is kept OUT of the claim and parked (GREEN board) rather than left in the claim (RED board) — the synthesis the escape-hatch principle requires ("parking beats lying" only holds if parking earns green). Luneth OK'd it explicitly.

- Per-type facet ORDER: conditions lead stance -> mechanism -> protocol -> warning (FACET_ORDER_BY_TYPE in core/schemas/search.ts; state facetGroups reads it by entity type); elements/poisons keep basics -> warnings. A disease page's compelling content is the cause+cure, not a diagnostic caution.

- "Also Tier-1" -> "RELATED" + ONE unified pill: renderPill(slug) is a clickable accent link iff getEntity(slug) != null, else a plain chip; used by BOTH the per-claim RELATED row and the per-entity RELATED list. Pills self-upgrade as entities are authored (Calcium is already orange/clickable on the Colloidal page; Chromium/Selenium grey until authored) -- structure decides, zero duplicated clickability logic. Three rules: (1) trail[0] is ALWAYS {tab:'home',label:'Home'} — replaces the old section-tab root that could go stale once you branch across essential↔condition; goCrumb() already routes a tab-crumb to close the detail, so the Home crumb exits cleanly to the Home tab. (2) A branch now findIndex()es the target crumb's key (crumbKey: tab:/stub:/k:s) in the trail — if it's already there it slice(0,dup+1)s back to it (jump-back) instead of concat()ing, which is what kills the infinite ping-pong growth. (3) capTrail() splices index 1 (the oldest recent crumb — never Home[0], never the current tail) until length ≤ CRUMB_MAX, i.e. Home + 5 most-recent; CRUMB_MAX is a one-line tunable (5–8) at line 418.

summary: Redesign D3-P2 chunk 1: built + signed off the unified "Ask Wallach" search — one box, split into Jump-to entities + In-the-books Q&A, with a discovery taster and a click-to-jump that flashes the exact claim on its page.
detail:
P2 is the "Ask Wallach" search — the second big piece of the redesign. It's one search box that, when you type, splits what it finds into two groups: "Jump to" (nutrients, conditions, topics — the fast lane to a page) and "In the books" (Wallach's actual questions-and-answers mined from his books — the delightful part). Empty, it shows a friendly taster of things to try. Click a book question and it takes you to that entity's page, opens the exact card, and briefly washes it green so you can see where you landed. Luneth signed it off after four quick rounds of feedback.

Prototype-only — temporary/knowledge-drawer-prototype.html (gitignored demo; no pillar/artifact/app code touched, board stays 53/53). It's a command-palette MODAL per blueprint §8.5 (centered 720px scrim+modal, ap-* namespace, design tokens only), opened via the green topbar "Ask Wallach" button / the rail item / "/" and closed via the app's normal .knh__close X + Esc + click-outside.

Mechanics: searchAll() (the existing live-suggest over ESS/CONDS/TOPICS) drives "Jump to" — family-coloured rows (nutrients green, conditions orange, topics violet), first-match highlighted. A new searchClaims() ranks the 198 mined faceted claims (all-words match over question+answer_short+subject+topics, with question/subject boosted) for "In the books", rendered as question title + one-line quick-answer + facet·book meta. Zero-query state = apDiscovery(): Try-asking chips (fill the search) + Common-conditions + Popular-essentials chips (open pages). Keyboard: ↑↓ across a flat apEls list, Enter opens, Esc closes, hover selects. Claim-jump: pendingClaimQ carries the clicked question through nav() (with detail=null so it roots a fresh Home › … trail); at the end of renderDetail(), apFlashPending() finds the .sr-claim whose .sr-claim__q text equals the question, opens the <details> + its parent facet, smooth-scrolls to center, and runs a ~1s ::after green wash over that card. Data injected as const CLAIMS/BOOKS (lean projection of search-index.json — 198 claims, 6 books).

Four feedback rounds, all landed: (1) eyebrow reworded from "6 books — not AI" to the user-facing "retrieval over Wallach's body of work"; (2) the ESC chip became a real close button, then — per Luneth — the app's normal .knh__close style rather than a bespoke red box; (3) the flash: first a per-card ring (too slow at 1.8s), then a full-screen green flash (my over-literal misread of "the whole thing" — it defeats the point of showing WHERE you are), corrected to a ~1s green wash over the box itself; (4) blur lag fixed — the cost was animating opacity/scale over a backdrop-filter element (it reblurs the whole viewport every frame), so the scrim's fade-in animation was removed (blur now computes once), scale/saturate dropped, blur 5→4px.

Verified headless with 2 dedicated puppeteer probes (split results + match-highlight + keyboard nav + open-lands-on-the-right-page; eyebrow text + X-button-closes + claim-jump-opens-and-flashes-the-EXACT-clicked-card), zero page errors, screenshots at every state. summary: Redesign D3-P2 chunk 2: the Ask-Wallach ranking/synonym pass — lay terms now resolve (blood sugar→Diabetes, quicksilver→Mercury, b12→Cobalt), results are tier-scored, and homosexuality/intersex never surface in search unless explicitly named. Signed off.
detail:
This is the second half of the "Ask Wallach" search: making it actually understand how people type. Before, you had to type the exact name; now the search knows Wallach's own everyday words for things — so "blood sugar" brings up Diabetes, "quicksilver" brings up Mercury, "b12" brings up Cobalt, "climate" brings up Carbon — and each result quietly notes which word matched ("via 'blood sugar'"). It also ranks results sensibly and, importantly, it will NOT show the homosexuality/intersex material unless someone explicitly searches those words — that content stays in the Explore index only. Luneth signed it off.

Prototype-only — temporary/knowledge-drawer-prototype.html (gitignored demo; no pillar/artifact/app code touched, board stays 53/53).

Data: re-injected CLAIMS carrying the full modern-voice `answer` text (real recall — fixes "sugar cravings", which lived in the answer body I'd dropped in chunk 1) + a resolved SEARCH_ENTITIES synonym table (the 56 search entities → {slug, name, k, syn}); all 56 resolve 1:1 to the browse ESS/CONDS/TOPICS (verified 0 misses), so synonyms attach to real pages.

Logic: replaced the crude all-words searchClaims with a tiered-scoring suite. apTier scores a field exact(6) › prefix(5) › word-start(4) › substring(3). nameTier weights the display name ×20, an exact element symbol =100 (so "cr" → Chromium ranks with a name-prefix, tie broken by claim count), slug words ×12. aliasTier weights a synonym ×16 (between name and slug). rankEntities scans ESS/CONDS/TOPICS by name + the SEARCH_ENTITIES synonyms, dedups by k:slug taking the max score, and tags synonym-sourced rows with a "via <synonym>" hint. rankClaims scores each claim question(12)/subject(9)/answer_short(6)/answer(4) with per-query-word coverage(+2 each) and a +8 subject-boost when the query hit an entity's name/synonym (so "blood sugar" boosts every diabetes claim). Both replace the old searchAll/searchClaims calls in apRender.

Charged-content gate (Luneth's explicit ask): CHARGED = {homosexuality, intersex}. chargedExplicit(q) marks a charged subject "explicitly named" only on a strong match — the entity name exact/prefix OR an EXACT synonym ("gay", "homosexual", "same-sex attraction", "lgbt"…), never an incidental substring. rankEntities filters charged entities out unless explicit; rankClaims skips charged-subject claims unless explicit. Result: "testosterone" and "sexual" no longer pull up homosexuality; "gay"/"homosexual"/"intersex" still do. The Explore tab is EXEMPT (it doesn't use these rankers) and remains the full categorised index.

Testosterone/strength reality check: the corpus genuinely has no "increase testosterone / get stronger" content yet — the only "testosterone" hits are incidental mentions inside aromatherapy/cholesterol/homosexuality claims, and sexual_health has just 1 claim. So that's a MINING gap, not a code gap; I did not fake mappings (anti-fakery). Two follow-ups captured for the search-mining phase: (1) proactively mine + tag general-interest lay topics people search — men's-health / strength / vitality with lay synonyms ("increase testosterone", "get stronger", "build muscle", "stamina", "virility") — the ranking machinery is ready and will light up the moment the data is tagged, exactly like "blood sugar" does now; (2) the charged-search-gate becomes doctrine (port to the real search build) + backfill missing synonyms like "lesbian" → homosexuality.

Verified headless: a ranking probe (blood sugar→Diabetes, quicksilver→Mercury, vitamin b12→Cobalt, cr→Chromium, sugar-cravings recall) + a gate probe (testosterone / how-to-increase-testosterone / sexual → NO homosexuality-or-intersex; gay / homosexual / intersex / same-sex attraction → shown), zero page errors, plus a screenshot of the "blood sugar → Diabetes (via 'blood sugar')" win. Plain: the redesign demos are all signed off, so this session planned how to actually build them into the real app — the hard part being to NOT drag the old system along and NOT let fake placeholder text sneak in. detail:
Installed the Phase-H "enforcement floor": three machine tripwires + their self-tests, landed BEFORE any redesigned surface so the migration cannot copy the prototypes' shortcuts into the shipped app. No app code, no user-facing change — pure guardrails.

Why floor-first: the signed-off prototypes deliberately inline prose and per-entity data as literals for speed. The migration risk is pasting those shortcuts into the real views. So the gates that forbid them go LIVE first; every later chunk then builds under them.

The three gates (tools/invariants.py, each = a thin path-binding check_* wrapper over a param-taking _impl so a negative test can drive the same logic — the amounts_wallach_only pattern):
1. views_no_inline_prose (R4 code-side) — RED on a prose-shaped string literal (>=12 words, or a sentence boundary in a >40-char run) inside a CLEAN view file. Clean-surface-scoped: _CLEAN_VIEW_FILES is EMPTY in H0 (no redesigned view exists yet -> vacuously green) and grows as each view is migrated (H2-H4). This is the honest, staged form of the blueprint's "scan views/+state/" — the current views are FULL of inline prose that only leaves when their view is replaced, so scanning them now would red the board; instead the gate binds the clean surface and widens.
2. entity_render_is_projection (R1) — RED on an object literal keyed by a real entity id, or a `slug === 'calcium'` content branch, inside the entity-render view. Closes the hole views_state_no_inline_data cannot see: a 2-key content map slips under its >10-element threshold. Scans against the real 947-id set (canon slugs + catalog condition/symptom ids + product ids). _ENTITY_VIEW_FILES empty in H0 (the render is built in H2).
3. no_stub_render_paths — RED on any prototype/demo scaffold token (kn-stub, sh-stub, "next chunk", "real build", "demo wires", PROTOTYPE, exemplar) in a shipped view (.ts) or stylesheet (.css). Active immediately (green today, verified: shipped surfaces carry none; the tokens live only in gitignored temporary/*.html). git-unavailable fails open LOUD.

Negative tests (R7 "codify, don't promise" — a gate is only trusted once proven to FIRE): tools/test_no_stub_render_paths.py (9/9: baseline+clean GREEN, all 7 tokens RED), tools/test_views_no_inline_prose.py (5/5: baseline+clean GREEN, 3 prose classes RED incl. the real cornerstone-quote sentence), tools/test_entity_render_is_projection.py (6/6: premise calcium+osteoporosis in id set, baseline+clean GREEN, unquoted-map + quoted-map + eq-branch RED).

No dashboard .ts touched -> dist unaffected by the gates themselves; no render probe (no surface). The gates' real scope widens as views migrate in H2-H4.

summary: Phase H1 chunk-2: pill-derivation fix + prominence + 2 gates — a condition now restores only nutrients Wallach ties to IT (directed maps(), no essentials[]-union leak); works_with=real interaction partners; base-line table rows kept out of the curated 'what to do' slot
detail:
Plain: on a condition's page, the list of "nutrients to restore" used to sweep in nutrients that Wallach actually ties to a DIFFERENT disease — because some claims name many diseases and many minerals at once, and the old code just merged them all together. Now a nutrient shows up for a disease only when Wallach genuinely links the two. Same fix on the essential pages: "works with" now means real interaction partners, not "everything ever mentioned in the same breath." And a plain reference row from Wallach's supplement TABLE (fluoride) no longer poses as a curated recommendation — which had absurdly put "fluoride" under a page that also says "avoid fluoride." Two automated guards make sure the leak can't come back.

Pill-derivation correctness + prominence (Phase H1 chunk-2, migration blueprint §4 H1 items (i) + (iii)).

THE DEFECT (Audit B): the "nutrients to restore" (condition) and "works with" (essential) pills were computed by flattening essentials[] across MULTI-condition claims. A claim like WAL-CLM-RARE-000275 (a 10-condition x 10-mineral Rare-Earths deficiency list) handed osteoporosis all 10 minerals, so Zinc/Chromium/Selenium/Tin/Vanadium (which map to diabetes/immunity/cancer/deafness, never osteoporosis) leaked onto the page.

THE FIX — one directed relation maps(E,C), drives both the green "restore" pills and the orange "help-with" pills:
- maps(E,C) holds iff a claim links E,C where kind is a directed prescription (protocol/dose — always), OR a focused nutrient<->condition tie (deficiency_sign/prognosis) that is NOT a "shotgun" (>=3 essentials AND >=3 conditions — a many-to-many list whose per-pair mappings can't be recovered).
- This resolves the audit cases AUTOMATICALLY: the 5 D2 misfits clear (they exist for osteoporosis only in the shotgun + interaction claims); phosphorus drops from "restore" (its only osteoporosis ties are mechanism/toxicity/interaction — it is a LIMIT, not a restore, and its toxicity claim still renders amber "signs"); vitamin-D's genuine 13-condition one-to-many list and umbrella protocols survive (not shotguns). Osteoporosis "restore" collapses 16(leaky) -> 8 clean: boron, calcium, germanium, magnesium, strontium, vitamins A/D/K — matching Wallach's actual protocol callout.
- "works with" (essential pages) = essentials sharing a kind='interaction' claim, NOT co-occurrence. Calcium -> {copper, magnesium, selenium, zinc} (its 3 real interaction claims), killing the "interacts with 41" inflation + the Gallium/Germanium/Tin/Oxygen phantoms.
- co-occurrence stays ONLY for the violet "keep exploring" + related-conditions (serendipity), where broad is correct.

PROMINENCE (item iii): corpus_embed.py now projects base_line_table (a claim tagged base-line-program / dose-table — a supplement-TABLE reference row, e.g. Fig. 8-1). entity_page_derive's protocol_claim_ids (the curated "what to do" source) EXCLUDES base-line-table dose rows, so a reference row never auto-fills a curated primary slot. Fluoride (WAL-CLM-LETS-000051) is out of osteoporosis's protocol slot.

summary: Phase H1 follow-up: split the flattened Table 7-8 corpus claim (RARE-000275) into 10 per-disease claims — recovers genuine ties (magnesium→hypertension, copper+sulfur→osteoporosis, boron→bone-spurs) without reopening the leak; sealed kv 320→321
detail:
Plain: this is the first of the two data fixes the H1 fan-out surfaced. Wallach has a table (Table 7-8) that maps each degenerative disease to the mineral deficiencies that cause it — osteoporosis to calcium/magnesium/boron/copper/sulfur, hypertension to calcium/magnesium/boron, cancer to selenium, and so on. But when it was first mined, the whole table got collapsed into ONE claim listing all 10 diseases and all 10 minerals together, which throws away which mineral goes with which disease. The H1 "restore pills" rule sees a claim that broad and refuses to guess (rightly — otherwise it would tie selenium to osteoporosis and calcium to cancer). So genuine ties silently vanished. The fix is to split that one claim back into one claim per disease, exactly as the table prints it. Now each disease's page shows the right minerals, and the safety rule never had to be weakened.

Table 7-8 split (Phase H1 follow-up · sealed-corpus mining · migration blueprint §1.2 over-correction class (a)).

THE PROBLEM: WAL-CLM-RARE-000275 ("Table 7-8. Common Degenerative Diseases and Their Cause", Rare Earths p.169) carried conditions=[10 diseases] × essentials=[10 minerals] as flat unions — the per-disease pairing was destroyed at mining time. It is the ONLY restore-kind "shotgun" claim in the whole corpus (≥3 essentials AND ≥3 conditions), so the H1 pill rule excluded it entirely, dropping 5 genuine ties: bone_spurs→boron, hypertension→magnesium+boron, osteoporosis→copper+sulfur. Confirmed by the H1 fan-out (wf_a7ea82b2-c73).

THE FIX (split, never loosen — [[flattened-table-claim-split-not-loosen]]): repurposed the original claim to osteoporosis-only + added 9 new per-disease claims (RARE-000303..000311), one per source row, so NONE is a shotgun (each maps exactly 1 condition):
  osteoporosis / arthritis ← Ca, Mg, B, Cu, S · hypertension / bone_spurs ← Ca, Mg, B · cancer / cardiomyopathy / cataracts ← Se · diabetes ← Cr, Va, Zn · aneurysm ← Cu · deafness ← Sn.
All 10 share the exact sealed full-table verbatim (313 chars). This was deliberate: corpus_verify's #2 forbids a verbatim under 60 chars, so bare rows ("Cancer: Se") are invalid; the full table is also faithful and self-explaining (its header decodes Se/Cr/etc.), and because it names every disease, verbatim_names_mapped_conditions holds for each single-condition claim. claim_text is per-disease plain prose with NO internal "Table 7-8" ref (internal_refs_out_of_prose); the "Table 7-8" attribution rides in the table-7-8 tag → view header.

TOOLING / ORDER (the mechanic that matters): corpus_extract finalize reads existing claims from the SHARD and OVERWRITES the draft, so the order was finalize (add 9) → mine_batch apply (edit the original in the draft) → corpus_seal. Pre-checks: all 6 book drafts == their shards before starting (clean; the seal promotes only this change) + no duplicate-offset constraint (corpus_verify #5 is duplicate-ID only). corpus_seal promoted draft→shard, re-derived indices, bumped knowledge_version 320→321, re-goldened 14 files; its final corpus_verify gate PASSED (1255 claims, 6 books, hashes match).

RESULT + VERIFICATION: hypertension restore → +magnesium +boron; osteoporosis restore → +copper +sulfur (8→10 pills); bone_spurs restore → +boron. Regenerated corpus-embed (kv=321) + entity-page-data + all MANIFEST artifacts. build OK (4537.0 KB); invariants 61/61 (entity_pills_justified 2568→2578, every pill still justified — the leak the shotgun rule closed stays closed; corpus_integrity kv=321; derived_artifacts_fresh in sync; verbatim_names_mapped_conditions 0 new; references_resolve green); render_probe_knowledge PASS (no regression). Reverts cleanly via git if needed (the seal changes are all committed).

detail:
The Knowledge drawer used to carry a persistent bar along its bottom with PIN, SHARE, CITE and EXPAND buttons. That bar is now gone. Underneath, PIN/SHARE/CITE were dead — they had no click handler at all, pure demo scaffold that shipped inert. Beyond being dead, SHARE and CITE fight what this app is: an offline-only, single-user, local-data instrument. SHARE presupposes a network + a recipient + an identity, none of which exist here (the honest "share" is JSON export or an OS screenshot); CITE is redundant because every claim already renders its Wallach book + page on the card. PIN is the only one with real local-first DNA (saving/bookmarking), but a global dead button is the wrong form — if we ever want it, it should be a per-entity star feeding a "Saved" view, built deliberately. EXPAND was the one wired button (it widened the 950px drawer), but Luneth chose to drop it too: 950px is already generous and a fixed width is simpler chrome.

Scope: Knowledge drawer ONLY. Journey (which is a planned full overhaul) and Search keep their own footers untouched — Journey's holds real actions (LOG EVENT + EXPORT), Search's holds a live count.

Technical:
- views/knowledge.ts — removed the <footer class="kd-footer"> markup (the 4 buttons + spacer) and every trace of its wiring: the toggleExpanded() function, the isExpanded state variable, the `expand` branch in the action handler, and the toggleExpanded member on the DrawerHandle interface + the bridge return object. In close(), dropped the now-unused kd-expanded from the classList.remove call. Fixed the file-header comment that still said "950px starting width, EXPAND grows to fill the workspace area" (a drifted comment is a defect, §00.B).
- drawer-knowledge.css — removed the dead `#drawer-knowledge-mount.kd-expanded { width: calc(100vw - 220px); }` width rule.
- drawer-shared.css — the footer/action CSS is SHARED with Journey via grouped selectors, so I stripped ONLY the `#drawer-knowledge-mount .kd-footer / .kd-action / .kd-action:hover / .kd-action__glyph / .kd-action__spacer` selectors from the 5 shared rules, keeping every `#drawer-journey-mount .jd-*` selector so Journey is visually unchanged.
- Kept `is-expanded` entirely — that is the best-sources "show more sources" toggle in the essentials deep-dive, a different mechanism from the EXPAND button.

Removal method: a single rule-5 safe_write script that read knowledge.ts once, applied every edit in memory with count assertions (exactly-one-occurrence), removed the glyph-bearing footer via regex (so the ⊕ ↗ ⌑ ⤢ glyphs never had to be hand-typed), asserted no stray toggleExpanded/isExpanded/kd-expanded/kd-footer/class="kd-action" remained, then rewrote once; the two CSS files the same way.

detail:

The app tracked the first half exhaustively and never surfaced the second — a lifelong follower couldn't tell if it even knew. This ships the fix: a dedicated, deliberately beautiful "Absorption" tab in the Knowledge drawer that makes the second prong impossible to miss.

summary: Topic pages: Absorption food cards now open as an overlay with a "Go back" button, the kicker "Explore" links to the all-topics grid, and every topic finally shows an at-a-glance intro; plus 4 food-summary fixes and a new gated intro_claim pointer.
detail:
The Knowledge drawer's topic pages got the three fixes Luneth asked for. (1) When you click a food card on the Absorption tab, the page now opens ON TOP of Absorption, so the back button reads "Go back" and returns you there -- before, it dumped you in the Explore grid. (2) The word "Explore" in every topic's little header is now a link that jumps to the all-topics list. (3) Every topic now shows a one-line intro at the top (29 of 58 had none); it's pulled from that topic's single best Wallach claim, so it's real and sourced, never invented. Then Luneth polished four food intros: beef and salt lost their awkward "Yes."/"No." openers, cholesterol now leads with Wallach's deficiency->disease point, and pork's over-reaching Amish summary was swapped for his clean "legitimate red meat" stance.

Mechanism: topic pages now render as a SHELL-LEVEL OVERLAY in views/knowledge.ts -- activeTab is no longer clobbered to 'explore', so the origin tab stays active and the back button/label follow it (tab==='explore' -> "All topics", else -> "Go back", new kt_back_generic copy). renderExploreTab() is grid-only; renderTopicPage(slug, fromExplore) threads the origin. A new explore-home action + .kt-kicker__link make the kicker "Explore" always jump to the grid. state/search::entityLede() derives every topic's lede from a type-aware facet priority (INTRO_ORDER_DEFAULT / _BY_TYPE[person] in core/schemas) -- basics-first, biography for people, biography+warning sunk for others (so fish does not front its FDA-petition biography) -- soft-clamped at 340 chars so chicken/pork's 650-char stance can't become an essay. A new OPTIONAL, derive-VALIDATED intro_claim pointer on a search entity overrides the derived pick with a named OWN-subject claim (cholesterol -> EPIGEN-000151, pork -> IMMORT-000229); search_index_derive.validate() REDs the board if the pointer is not that entity's own enriched claim (negative-gated). Content faithfulness: beef HELLS-000001 + salt RARE-000312 were opener trims only (verbatims unchanged); cholesterol was REPOINTED because its Weston-Price stance verbatim could not carry the deficiency->disease line, whereas EPIGEN-000151's verbatim literally lists Alzheimer's, type-2 diabetes, ED, low-T, menopause and adrenal exhaustion; pork was repointed away from the Amish claim whose 4%/6%/wood-ashes summary over-reached its thin sealed verbatim (that verbatim only says the Amish eat meat 3x/day). Gates: build clean (tsc+esbuild), invariants 62/62 (derived_artifacts_fresh + search_index_wellformed confirm the re-derived index and the new intro_claim check), render_probe_knowledge PASS with 4 NEW assertions (foods->"Go back"+returns-to-Absorption, explore->"All topics", kicker link->grid, a no-basics food shows a derived intro), 6 hero screenshots reviewed. detail:
Luneth wanted to try dropping EVERY serif font and going fully futuristic to honor the "Empower" reference. The warm cream paper, the orange accent, and the mono readouts all stayed. One deliberate exception: the crown-jewel Wallach quote in the Absorption tab keeps the old elegant Playfair serif as the single serif accent. We did it as a reversible override LAYER (one CSS file + the font + one link) so the sealed design-system.css is untouched and nothing risky happened; the proper fold-in plus a full audit of remaining serif spots is next session's font survey.

Mechanism: dashboard/assets/styles/type-futurist.css is loaded LAST in dashboard.html. The sealed design-system.css + its golden are DELIBERATELY untouched -- its Playfair/Merriweather/Crimson tokens are SUPERSEDED (documented in the file header + the handoff), NOT authoritative, pending the next-session FONT SURVEY that (a) audits every remaining serif instance across the app, (b) confirms carve-outs, (c) folds the direction into design-system.css + re-seals the golden, (d) retires type-futurist.css. Verified live via headless screenshots of Coverage (THE WHOLE PICTURE, 9-of-90 counter, periodic-table symbols, DAILY PROTOCOL) + Absorption (hero, deck, villi diagram + Playfair pull-quote, 115M stat, 01/02 numerals). summary: Purged the dead Corpus + Doctrine tab code that survived UI-removal + multiple audits, and wired knip as a critical dead-code gate on the invariants board so orphaned code can never ship silently again (proven with a negative test).
detail:
Fixes a recurring, trust-damaging failure: code from features that were "deleted" kept physically living in the repo, because removing a tab from the UI is a different operation than deleting its code — and no gate ever checked. Luneth caught the Corpus tab's Wallach quote still living in the source ~24h and 10+ sessions after the tab was cut. I removed the specific corpses AND, more importantly, wired the missing gate so new dead code can no longer ship without turning the board red.

REMOVED (views/knowledge-corpus.ts, 645→429 lines): renderCorpusTab + book-browser chain (renderBookDeep, renderBookRow, renderPlannedRow, authorLabel, bookCountHTML) + the old Essentials-deep-dive renderCorpusForEssential / renderIntakeMeter / fmtAmount / CORPUS_KIND_PRIORITY / corpusKindOrder. The live Conditions tab + tileOf + the shared renderCorpusClaim/dose/Fig-8-1 graph were preserved (call graph mapped first; a byte-preserving anchor-asserted line-delete, not a hand rewrite). Their now-dead state tail (getClaimsForBook, listBooksWithId, listPlannedBooks) removed from state/corpus.ts (knip's iterative detection surfaced them once the views were gone). DELETED core/schemas/doctrine.ts + assets/data/doctrine-data.json + EVERY reference: the schema barrel export (schemas/index.ts), the eden/derived/MANIFEST.json registry entry, and invariants.py's _CLEAN_SURFACE_STORES entry + the body prose-home key + 2 stale comments.

ROOT CAUSE (the real answer to "why did all the rules never catch it"): every invariant targets DATA, never dead CODE; ESLint doesn't flag unused EXPORTS; and data_artifacts_accounted proved doctrine-data.json was TRACKED, not USED (green board, actively auditing a corpse). knip WAS a package.json devDep — but unconfigured, so a bare run flagged the entire codebase as dead (36 "unused files" incl. main.ts) = pure noise = never actionable = never enforced, and it only lived in an uninstalled pre-push hook, never on the round-close board. The detector existed; nothing ran it as a gate. "Don't leave dead code" had been a WISH the whole time.

FIX: dashboard/knip.json (entry = main.ts + tests, ignoreExportsUsedInFile) gives a true signal; no_new_dead_code (critical) in tools/invariants.py runs knip vs dashboard/knip-baseline.json (48 accepted migration-scaffold keys — the ratchet may only SHRINK). NEGATIVE TEST: injected a dead export → board went RED with the exact key → reverted → green (the gate has teeth, not another WISH).

VERIFIED: tsc clean · eslint clean · node tools/build.mjs OK · 63/63 invariants · render probes knowledge/coverage/adopt PASS (0 page errors — the gutted file still drives the Conditions tab, entity deep-dives, gloss tooltips). DEFERRED (honest, not hidden): burn down the 48 baselined scaffold items (8 state helpers reserved for pending rounds + 40 zero-runtime zod z.infer type aliases) deliberately over time; each is documented in the baseline, none is silent.

summary: Coverage Phase 2 — the plate language: covered essentials now LIFT off a machined substrate as white green-rimmed plates (orange was the app's own chrome colour, so the win was camouflaged); partial shows its real delivered÷target fill; purged 6 dead selector families
detail:
Coverage's states used to read as noise, and there was a precise reason. "Covered" was painted in the SAME orange the whole app uses for its ambient chrome — the scan line, the border travel, the buttons, the scrollbar, the pulse dot, the section numbers. The win state was camouflaged in brand paint. Meanwhile "gap" was --ds-status-warn amber (#c79830), sitting right beside that orange (#ff7e3c) on the colour wheel, so the win and the problem were the same colour family. "Partial" was #fffbf2 on #faf5e8 — a four-value delta, which is to say invisible. Nothing could feel satisfying because nothing was distinguishable.

Now coverage IS elevation. A covered essential's plate lifts off a recessed machined substrate — white, green-rimmed, carrying the white top-light — the way the plates lift off the underwiring in Luneth's Empower calibration reference. Sizing, fonts, grid and placement are byte-identical; only colour and depth changed, exactly per the contract he set.

GREEN WAS NEVER AN INVENTION. The Knowledge drawer ALREADY spoke green/amber/red/blue for these exact states (drawer-knowledge.css .kd-cov-dot--*). Coverage was the outlier teaching a contradictory language for one snapshot, and --ds-status-ok was already sitting in the sealed token set, unused by this surface. Luneth's "I'm thinking green" was the rest of his own app. Equally: removing orange from 90 tiles RESTORES the reference's rule rather than breaking it — the reference says "bright orange as a signal accent, not a wash," and painting 90 tiles orange WAS the wash. Orange now rides the winner as a signal tick and owns interaction/hover.

THE STATES. Dormant = sunk into the substrate, quiet and unlit — a fresh start must be restful, never a wall of red (Luneth was explicit). Gap = the same recess plus ONE 3px amber edge tick: a signal, not an alarm. Partial = mid-lift with a green FILL LEVEL whose height is the snapshot's real fillPercent (delivered ÷ Wallach target) — a number computed on every recompute since Phase C and thrown away by every consumer until now; verified rendering live at 42%. Present = lifted but hollow with a tech-blue rim, matching the drawer (it previously had ZERO Coverage CSS and rendered identical to pending). Covered = fully lifted, white→ok-wash, ok-bright rim, green drop shadow.

CARD TYPES. One shared plate chassis, four silhouettes via clip-path chamfers — vitamin cuts the top-right, amino the bottom-left, fat both, mineral stays square. Straight off the reference plates, at zero layout cost.

Variant A (Luneth's pick) is live behind a one-value toggle (--cov-strip-mode / [data-covered-variant='b']), verified flipping live. Kept deliberately: the A/B was judged on a mockup, and the real page at 90-tile density is the only honest test of whether the saturated strip becomes a wall.

The green scale (--ds-ok-deep/-bright/-wash, mirroring the accent scale's shape) is declared LOCALLY here, NOT in the sealed design-system.css — the same interim pattern type-futurist.css used for the Unbounded pivot. It folds into the sealed canonical with the pending font fold-in, under Luneth's sign-off and a golden re-seal.

(1) The orange tick was pinned to top/right:0, exactly where the vitamin and fat chamfers SLICED it into a glitch-looking sliver — now inset 13px past the deepest chamfer. Screenshots are the gate; exit codes are not.

NOT a clipping bug (a probe walked every ancestor: nothing clips; tile tops sit 93px inside .essentials-host). CAUSE: box-shadow paints FIRST-LISTED ON TOP, and I listed the white "top-light" (inset 0 1px 0) BEFORE the rim (inset 0 0 0 1px) — the light painted straight over the rim's top edge and erased it.
