  - scratchpad Puppeteer probe across 5 accents (ember, amethyst, teal, rose, slate): getComputedStyle + real page.hover, colours canvas-normalised so oklab() and color(srgb ...) serialisations compare equal → ALL PASS. pf-done and rc-restore resolve to the saturated hot rgb; the delete border resolves to the red err-mix (identical across accents, i.e. accent-independent, and not equal to the pale accent-deep).

summary: Removed-item Restore button reads on hover again in dark (deepen the tint, keep bright text, readable on all 8 accents); reverted last round's misfire on the wrong button (.rc-btn-restore).
detail:
Luneth reported that hovering a removed-item "Restore" button in the recycle bin made its text almost unreadable on every dark accent. This is the correct fix -- and it also corrects a misfire from earlier today.

What went wrong first: last round I "fixed" .rc-btn-restore, which is the deleted-SAVES restore pill -- the WRONG button. His words were "ONLY for removed items", and removed items use a different (ghost) button class, .rc-btn-ghost. Worse, my earlier change hurt the deleted-saves button's own hover contrast, so I reverted it.

The real bug: in dark, dark block (G) lifts the ghost button's text to --ds-accent-bright so it reads on its resting translucent wash. But (G)'s :is() selector carries specificity (0,5,0), so it also governs the :hover state. The base :hover (workspace-regimen.css) FILLS the background with the solid accent colour -- and bright-accent text on a solid-accent fill is accent-on-accent, roughly 1:1 contrast (worst on amethyst: purple text on purple). Invisible.

The fix (J8, theme.css, dark-only):
  :root[data-theme="dark"] .rc-item .rc-btn-ghost:hover {
    background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-accent) 32%, transparent);
    border-color: var(--ds-accent);
  }
Instead of filling solid, the hover DEEPENS the translucent tint and solidifies the border, keeping the dark theme's bright-text-on-dark regime. That keeps the bright text readable on all 8 accents. I first tried a single fixed light text (#fffbf2) but it washes out on the pale accents (measured gold 2.06, ember 2.45, teal 2.54 -- below even bold-AA); the deepened-tint approach avoids that entirely.

Reverted: J6's .rc-btn-restore:hover -> --ds-accent-hot change from commit 88acd1a3. That button carries dark --ds-paper-light text (#221d15 in dark), so saturating its hover fill actually dropped its text contrast from ~7.5 to ~2.3. Restoring the original --ds-accent-deep hover is better for it. J6 is now the .pf-done fix only.

A verification lesson: my first recycle probe INJECTED a top-level .rc-btn-restore button and reported a false PASS. A synthetic proxy at the document root is not the real element in its real container -- and it also let me test the wrong class without noticing. The honest check drove the ACTUAL recycle popup (seeded the bin through the real removal bridge, opened it, hovered the real button) and screenshotted it.

Verification:
  - node tools/build.mjs -> exit 0
  - invariants 92/92
  - recycle render probe PASS (0 page errors)
  - real-popup Puppeteer probe across all 8 accents: hover contrast (accent-bright text vs the 32% tint composited over the popup surface) = 3.46 to 4.98; worst is amethyst 3.46 (bold-AA), most are full AA. Amethyst + gold hover screenshots reviewed: bright readable text, deepened tint, solid border.

Correction of record: the 15:01 build-log line and its Creator's Log entry credited the .rc-btn-restore change with fixing "the recycle Restore hover". That was the wrong button and is now reverted; the actual reported bug (the removed-ITEM ghost button) is fixed here.

  On a condition's detail page, the main content box + the small category icon had their BORDERS tinted the accent (amethyst) in dark, even though the icon's own colour correctly followed the condition's category (Cancer grey, Osteoporosis blue, Anemia red). The borders now follow --cat too, matching the icon and the light theme.

My first override still lost, because the dark "drawers" block has an accent-deep :is() override whose :is() specificity is (1,4,0) -- it TIED my override and won on source order (it sits later in the file). (Note for next time: :is() takes the specificity of its most specific argument, so an :is() list that contains a two-class selector is (1,2,0)+prefix, not (1,1,0)+prefix.)

Two things shipped this chunk. First, the 155 "Dead Doctors Don't Lie" claims that were stuck OUT of search: each was flagged because its quote didn't literally name the condition it was filed under. Second, a bug Luneth caught: the condition detail pages were the ONLY place still showing raw claim cards, while Ask Wallach (and the essential + explore-topic pages) showed the enriched question-and-answer format. summary: The label Scanner got tougher and clearer: gluten grains and oats plus ALL artificial food dyes are now hard rejects, seed/fried oils reject unless the product still delivers 3+ real nutrients, and every verdict now names the exact ingredient it flagged.
detail:
You scan a food label; the Scanner judges it against Wallach and says Add / Neutral / Reject. Nine refinements today made it stricter where Wallach is strict, and made its reasons impossible to misread.

WHAT CHANGED. (1) Oats now REJECT just like wheat, barley and rye -- they are all gluten grains -- unless the label carries a 'gluten free oats' declaration (the one exception). 'Organic oats' used to slip through as neutral; not anymore. (2) Seed / fried oils (canola, soybean, sunflower, etc.) now REJECT on their own, BUT if the whole product still delivers at least 3 real nutrients in meaningful amounts, the oil is 'offset' and the verdict softens to NEUTRAL (never a recommendation). (8) ALL artificial food dyes are now a HARD reject -- a brand-new 'artificial dyes' list with 181 exact spellings (Red 40, Yellow 5, Blue 1, Tartrazine, the FD&C forms, the European E-numbers, the international azo dyes, the CI colour-index codes). Wallach DOES back this: in Let's Play Doctor his hyperactivity treatment is the Feingold diet -- 'avoid sugar, additives, food colors' (WAL-CLM-LETS-000305) -- so no source-rule override was needed. I researched the full dye list and guarded hard against mis-fires: bare 'Amaranth' (a grain) is matched only via its dye codes, and 'Green S'/'Orange B' can't bleed into 'Green Salad'/'Orange Blossom'. detail: When I removed the obsolete grey hint under the ingredients box, the box moved from full-width (below the upload zone) into a narrow right-hand column — a regression Luneth caught. Cause: the scan row is a flex-wrap layout; the upload zone has a fixed-ish flex basis but the ingredients box had none, so its width came from its content. The long hint paragraph was quietly making the box wide enough to wrap onto its own full-width row; deleting the hint shrank it, so it stopped wrapping and squeezed in beside the upload zone. Fix: pin the ingredients box to full width ('flex: 1 1 100%') so it always takes its own row regardless of content. I finished landing the Immortality book into the live corpus. summary: Landed the Epigenetics book — 17 Wallach claims now live, completing the 5-book unverified-landing campaign (every Wallach book is now front-facing and searchable).
detail:
Epigenetics was the last of five “unverified” Wallach books whose ruled claims we’ve been landing one book at a time. With it live, all of Wallach’s in-housed books now surface in Ask-Wallach search. The memorable part of this one: the book itself misspells a real person’s name — Lydia Pinkham (of the famous Vegetable Compound) is printed “Pinkums” throughout. The rule here is that we keep Wallach’s genuine claims even when they disagree with the mainstream, but we DO fix clear typos and misspelled names using outside knowledge — so “Pinkums” became “Pinkham” (and its possessive “Pinkham’s”), and I wrote the change into the divergences ledger so a future page-check won’t “correct” it back to the book’s error.

kv 486→490; sealed WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000481..497 (17 claims). Pipeline: assemble keeps → question + claim_text dedup vs sealed → screenshot vision fleet → condition-mapping remediation → seal sequence.

DISPOSITIONS. Dropped proposed 525 (byte-identical claim_text to already-live 469, iodine+copper→varicose veins; the recovery’s own dedup marked it FRESH — the manual claim_text-vs-sealed pass is what caught it). Keep-both: proposed 524→sealed 484 (menopause/history) twins already-live 479 on the same Lydia-Pinkham passage; Luneth ruled keep-both and 484 was given a distinct claim_text (the ‘what women used before modern medicine’ framing vs 479’s ‘what the remedy was’). Added the pair to _DUPLICATE_KEEP_BOTH with a pinned test, and reconciled a pre-existing drift found in passing: {HELLS-101,HELLS-102} was in the allowlist but missing from that test’s membership pin (left by the HK landing; the test isn’t one of the 94 board gates, so it had gone red unnoticed) — pin corrected 74→76.

VISION. 12-agent screenshot fleet, one per book page, book on the LEFT ~48% of the dual-monitor captures. 15 VERIFIED-CLEAN, 2 ‘DEFECTS’ — both the Lydia passage, where our purified .txt was ALREADY cleaner than the recovered candidate (candidate carried alled/amenorthea; our source already read called/amenorrhea). Source .txt corrections, all page-true and re-snapped (0 BROKEN): Pinkums→Pinkham x4 (incl. back-matter index) + magazine adds→ads + possessive Pinkums’→Pinkham’s (book_typo_divergences); 521 stray-period ‘adrenal.’→‘adrenal’, 526/535 etc.), 535 4~6→4–6 en-dash, 517 Legg-<nl>Perthe hyphen-split (kept the real hyphen, dropped the line-break newline).

CATALOG. Sealed one condition synonym: menorrhagia += ‘heavy or more frequent menstrual periods’ / ‘heavy menstrual periods’ / ‘heavy periods’ (with_synonyms 144→145) so 539 (‘could a thyroid problem be behind my heavy periods?’) maps to the menorrhagia page. The exact phrase is required because the matcher does a contiguous substring test on the stopword-stripped verbatim.

MAPPING. Conditions mapped where the quote names them, else search-only per the approved remediation policy. 3 claims fully search-only, subject-routed: 483 boron (ED/testosterone), 486 cobalt (hypothyroidism), 496 peripheral_neuropathy (ergot skin-tingling). 485 was re-subjected rosacea→malabsorption to clear a duplicate-card collision with 497 (556, rosacea/mechanism) before sealing.

summary: Fixed two dark-mode cards that rendered as washed-out light boxes (Calcium + Omega-9), reworded a stale “no dose” message, and added a “why this number?” hover to all 30 remaining dosed nutrients — each tracing its target to a Wallach book. Board 94/94.
detail:
Four fixes this round, all on the offline dashboard. Two were dark-mode display bugs where a card showed up as a pale light box with unreadable text; one was an out-of-date sentence; and the big one gave every nutrient with a Wallach dose a little “why this number?” tooltip that explains, in one line, which book the number came from and how it was worked out.

DARK WASHOUT (Calcium “Absorbable calcium” card + Omega-9 note panel). Root cause: theme.css has four per-category dark blocks (:root[data-theme=“dark”] .kd-essential-deep[data-category=…], lines ~691–706) that remap --ds-accent and --ds-accent-deep but never remapped --ds-accent-wash / --ds-accent-soft. drawer-knowledge.css defines LIGHT category washes (mineral --ds-accent-wash:#e3edf7; fatty_acid color-mix(--fam-story 13%,#fff)) at specificity (1,2,0), which out-specifies the systemic dark remap (block A, :root[data-theme=dark], (0,2,0)). So in dark the wash stayed light, and any surface that FILLS with it read as a light box with the light cream text on top: calcium’s .kd-ep-fam__step--turn gradient (linear-gradient(165deg, var(--ds-accent-wash), var(--ds-paper-light))) and omega’s .kd-ep-mirror--aside background (var(--ds-accent-wash)). Fix: added translucent --ds-accent-wash: color-mix(--ds-accent 16%, transparent) and --ds-accent-soft: color-mix(--ds-accent 34%, transparent) to all four dark category blocks, mirroring block (A) so a wash fill composites as a subtle dark tint. Also brightened the omega --aside eyebrow (Luneth: “too dark”) to color-mix(--ds-accent 60%,#fff), scoped to :root[data-theme=dark] .kd-ep-mirror--aside .kd-ep-mirror__eyebrow. Verified via headless dark screenshots (calcium + omega fixed; vitamin-A + an amino page unregressed since those categories were touched too).

COPY. view-copy.json ep_no_target changed from “No Wallach maintenance number for this one yet — an honest gap until his dose tables are fully mined.” to “No fixed daily amount — Wallach never states an exact number for this one. For a practical guide to daily intake, see the recommended products below.” Confirmed on-screen that only the 12 amino acids hit this fallback and each renders a Best-Youngevity-sources list below, so “the recommended products below” always resolves (the structural elements carbon/hydrogen/nitrogen/oxygen route to a separate “None needed” present-treatment).

WHY-NUMBER. The hover mechanism already existed (essentialWhy(slug) → .kd-ep-why/.kd-ep-tip in renderAtAGlance) but only 6 of 37 dosed essentials had the copy. Authored the remaining 30 into entity-copy.json (phosphorus excluded — its book figure resolves to no on-screen number, so 30 not 31). Each blurb was generated from the sealed essentials-targets provenance plus the live displayed target read off the DOM — no number hand-typed — and follows the existing 5’s voice: 8 bodyweight-scaled minerals (Epigenetics per-100-lb table ×1.54 to a 154 lb adult); 7 flat minerals (LPD Base Line: sodium/sulfur/chloride/tin; Immortality: potassium; DDDL: germanium/silver); 15 vitamins from Epigenetics daily-multiple recommendations + LPD (folic acid, inositol), including the vitamin-D (40 IU per mcg) and vitamin-E (0.67 mg per IU) IU→mass conversions. IMPORTANT non-defect noted: the derive-layer JSON range field holds the RAW pre-scale book figure (e.g. boron 1–6), while the app displays the scaled value (boron 9.2 mg) — checked on the real screen, the existing 5 blurbs match their displayed numbers; no contradiction.

NEW GATE (§00.B). tools/render_probe_why_targets.js opens every essential that carries a why and asserts the tooltip renders and literally contains the on-screen target number — the truth anchor against why↔target drift (the number lives in two places: the coverage-computed target and the entity-copy prose). It is a render probe, not one of the 94 board invariants (the board is Python-only and cannot render the scaled/converted target), so it is honestly labeled as such.

summary: Phase 2 of the public cleanup: every README/comment brought current with the pristine tree, root README rewritten for public, and 3 chronicle record-dirs (contradictions/decisions/proposals) restored as cited provenance. Board 94/94, no functionality change.
detail:
Second and final phase of the pristine-for-public cleanup: the documentation pass. No code behavior changes — this brings the words in line with the tree and finishes the record-vs-scratch call.

RESTORED THREE RECORD-DIRS. Phase 1 deleted all of chronicle/ except the ledger, but the audit found contradictions/, decisions/ and proposals/ are cited ~12x by gates, derive tools and data files as the ratified-decision provenance for the hardest §00.A calls (cobalt→B12, the omega EFA 9 g group dose, omega-9 not arachidonic), and contradictions/ is the home CLAUDE.md’s conflict-logging rule points to. Luneth ruled restore. chronicle/ is now the durable ledger plus those record dirs — 33 files, down from 361 — with the transient scratch (header-research, theme-studies, ratify worked-records, audits, blueprints) gone.

PUBLIC README. Rewritten from scratch: removed the mid-overhaul framing and the links to the deleted OVERHAUL-BLUEPRINT and next-chunk; corrected the directory glossary to the real six top-level dirs (the old README named components/ and knowledge/, which no longer exist, and called the Products pillar “not yet built” though it is live); added a plain not-medical-advice note; and replaced the old “the book texts are kept here — this repository is private” paragraph with an honest account of why the copyrighted book texts are NOT distributed and how the board still runs without them.

DANGLING REFS. Every reference to a genuinely-deleted thing was fixed: design-wisdom (the retired capture library) across the element-headers skill, STYLE-GUIDE, two CSS comments and eden/corpus/README; the superseded build-dashboard.sh; two deleted blueprints cited from code; next-chunk cited as a durable record (repointed to the commit); the retired frontface subscript scanner. The one left in place is a dated calibration comment inside the hash-sealed design-system.css — editing it would break the seal, and it reads as 2026-06-21 provenance, so it is flagged rather than touched.

RULES→SKILLS. The project moved its doctrine from .claude/rules/*.md to .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md on 2026-08-03, but many comments still cited the old location. Repointed the doctrine-location citations across eden/README, dashboard.css, coverage_layout_derive.py, mining-coverage.json and several invariants.py comments — while leaving the rules-audit gate’s deliberate legacy-form handling (it exists to catch exactly this kind of stale pointer). Also deleted the vestigial eden/SCHEMA.md and eden/README’s dead “Vestigial” section.

LOCAL SCRATCH. Cleaning two vestigial .gitignore rules un-ignored 86 local leftover files — copyrighted page scans under a ratify dir and frontface OCR working files. Both were already untracked, regenerable, and backed up, so they were deleted from disk. next-chunk.md is now local-only (gitignored).

summary: Fixed the README gaps Luneth caught: deleted the obsolete root schemas/, restructured the main README to lead with a plain-English user guide, added the 3 missing folder READMEs (.claude/chronicle/dashboard), and cleared the leftover Phase-F staleness. Board 94/94.
detail:
A correction pass after Luneth reviewed the documentation cleanup and found real gaps I had missed — the prior pass fixed dangling references but did not freshen every README’s CONTENT or add the folder READMEs, and I had over-claimed “all READMEs updated”.

SCHEMAS. The root schemas/ (products-db.schema.json + versions.schema.json) is obsolete now that the eden pillars own validation — nothing live references it (only a 2026-06-22 build-log mention). Deleted, and removed from the README directory glossary.

ROOT README, restructured for a non-technical reader as Luneth specified: a plain-English intro, how to open it (double-click dashboard.html — offline, no install, no login), how to set yourself up (the welcome veil asks your name once, or “just browsing”, everything stays on-device), and what each of the five pages does (Coverage, Regimen, Scanner, Search/Ask-Wallach, Knowledge) — THEN the developer architecture/build/layout — THEN the disclaimers. This also corrected an error I had carried forward: both the old README and my first rewrite named a “Journey” surface and a “Command Palette” that do not exist; the real rail (WorkspaceTarget in main.ts) is Coverage · Regimen · Scanner · Search · Knowledge.

THREE MISSING FOLDER READMEs added — .claude/ (settings + skills + baseline), chronicle/ (the ledger + the ratified-decision docs), and dashboard/ (the app shell, the core→state→views layering, the sealed vs themeable stylesheets, the generated data).

PHASE-F STALENESS. Phase F has long landed and catalog/nutrients.json is live, but several docs still described the nutrient vocabulary as “deferred/dormant until Phase F”: fixed tools/README (which also said invariants was “currently 41” — it is 94 — and carried a Vestigial section for a file that no longer exists), eden/catalog/README, eden/README, and eden/products/README.

VERIFIED: node tools/build.mjs OK; invariants.py 94/94; render probes pass; a full README sweep confirms no stale forward-references remain. The documentation is now genuinely current and the top of the README is usable by a non-technical reader.

summary: Public-release cleanup: READMEs rewritten from the code, ~1,000 stale comments corrected across 280 files, dead modules removed, tools/ restructured, MIT licence added. Board 94/94, all 42 tests pass, probes 35/37 identical to baseline. Nothing in the app changed.
detail:
The repository is being made public, so this pass was about making it honest and
presentable rather than adding features. Nothing about how the dashboard behaves changed.

Three things happened. The READMEs were rewritten from the code itself: the old root README
described a bundled browser that was never built, and told you to "open the Profile page"
without saying it is the avatar in the bottom-left corner. Every number in the new one was
re-derived from the data before it was written down. Second, roughly a thousand stale or
misleading comments were corrected across 280 files -- comments that named deleted files,
counted things wrong, or explained the work in terms of internal sessions nobody outside
this project could follow. Third, tools/ was given a real structure: it had 96 loose files
in one folder, 79 of them tests and probes.

METHOD. Two read-only audit fleets (22 agents each) covered every tracked file and all
14,969 comment lines in the repo. Their 1,706 findings were merged, partitioned by file so
no two writers could collide, and applied by a 17-agent fleet: 941 applied, 83 rejected
after the applying agent checked the claim and found it false, 100 escalated as code
problems rather than prose.

DEAD CODE. core/eden.ts, core/source-rule.ts and views/palette.ts each had exactly one
referrer -- a dead import in main.ts held alive by a `_refs` bag and `void _refs`. Removing
that bag turned the no_new_dead_code gate RED on four exports it had been MASKING from knip
(a namespace import marks every export used). storage.get, storage.estimateUsage,
scanner.getLastScan and scanner.getLastResult were all confirmed dead and removed. The gate
had been green because of the defect. Also deleted assets/data/versions-data.json, whose
own _purpose named tools/version_bump.py -- a file that does not exist.

A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING. After moving the five design libraries out of the app,
vendor_assets_pinned printed OK while checking ZERO libraries. Its manifest path is built
from segments -- ROOT / "dashboard" / "assets" / "vendor" / "libs" -- which a string-level
path rewrite cannot see, so the gate found nothing and passed vacuously. The identical trap
sat in render_probe_mech_shape via path.join(REPO,'tools','goldens',...). Both were found by
asking the gate what it had actually checked instead of trusting its OK. It now verifies 5
of 5. Segmented paths are invisible to text substitution; check them by hand after any move.

REAL DEFECTS FIXED. invariants.py's _DUPLICATE_KEEP_BOTH literal contained two duplicate
frozenset keys, so Python silently kept the later, thinner entry and discarded the richer
one -- 78 literals collapsing to 76 keys. The same two pairs were duplicated in
test_no_duplicate_claims.py, whose printed label hardcoded "expect=76" and so agreed with
itself; it now derives the count. Two negative-control tests wrote their fixtures to
chronicle/ paths the gates never read, so both had been passing vacuously for weeks --
repointed to tools/gate-fixtures/, and both now genuinely exercise their gate.

PUBLIC-REPO HYGIENE. .claude/settings.json hardcoded one machine's absolute path in all
four hook commands. That leaked a username and, worse, meant every enforcement hook was
dead on anybody else's clone. It now uses ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, confirmed as the
documented and Windows-supported form. .claude/settings.local.json turned out to be ignored
only by the machine's global gitconfig, so a fresh clone would have committed it. .gitignore
carried four rules for folders that no longer exist and claimed to ignore the vendored OCR
engine while all six of its files were tracked -- a line that would silently have dropped a
new Tesseract file. eden/fringe-knowledge/ is now local-only, and the three documents that
pointed at it say so. An MIT LICENSE was added, with a scope note carving out the books, the
OFL fonts and the vendored libraries.

VERIFIED. Build OK. Invariants 94/94, zero failed. All 42 control tests pass from their new
home under tools/tests/. Render probes 35/37 -- byte-identical to the baseline captured
before any change was made; render_probe_group_dots and render_probe_orac failed before this
chunk too, and both were confirmed to be STALE PROBES rather than app faults
(render_probe_orac asserts .kd-orac-dec and .kd-orac-tbl, which appear nowhere in the source
or the stylesheets; render_probe_group_dots hardcodes a goal-to-group snapshot the sealed
layout has since moved past -- more-energy legitimately names the plant-derived group now,
along with 19 other goals).

DEFERRED AND REPORTED, NOT CHANGED. views/coverage.ts:112 maps a slug to the tile's DISPLAY
name while the coverage snapshot is keyed by the canonical name, so 16 tiles -- all twelve
vitamins plus folate, flavonoids and the three omegas -- can never enter the no-goal wanted
set, and no vitamin gap can pull a recommendation. entity-page.ts:816 renders "34
plant-derived elements" where the data says 35. The knowledge-foods pH ladder cites its
blood band to Dead Doctors Don't Lie when the claim belongs to Rare Earths, which is a
source-rule question rather than a cleanup one. scanner.ts:139 tells the user to check their
connection for a failure that cannot occur on file://. main.ts:416 logs a console warning
naming a product version on every boot. About 400 lines of CSS were verified dead but left
in place because deleting them is a visual risk that deserves eyes. safe_write.py's
post-write discipline check names two gates that no longer exist, so its rollback can never
fire. And eden/tools/purity-status.json lists six of the seven books, leaving Hell's
Kitchen's source text unchecked by that gate -- deliberately NOT guessed, because whether
that OCR is raw or pristine is a factual claim about the book, not something to infer.

summary: Fixed a Coverage join bug that made vitamin gaps invisible to the no-goal recommender: the lookup matched the tile display name, not the canonical name, silently dropping 16 of 91 tiles. New negative control pins it.
detail:
With no goals selected, Coverage turns the gaps showing on the board back into
nutrient ids so the recommender knows what to aim at. That lookup was matching on the
label printed on the tile rather than the nutrient's canonical name -- and for 16 of the
91 those are different strings. Every vitamin was silently skipped, so a vitamin gap
could never produce a product suggestion. Nothing went red, because the mineral gaps
resolved fine and the rail still filled with cards.

views/coverage.ts::slugToTileKey mapped slug -> t.name (the DISPLAY name), while a
CoverageSnapshot tile carries the layout tile's `key` -- the canonical target name --
per state/coverage.ts:262. wantedSlugs() lower-cased both sides, which rescued the 75
tiles that differ only in case and concealed the rest. The 16 that diverge further are
all twelve vitamins plus folate, flavonoids and the three omegas: 'RETINOL' was being
matched against 'Vitamin A (Retinol / beta-carotene)'. views/regimen.ts:188 already
mapped to t.key and was right all along; coverage.ts now matches it.

The proof is a negative control rather than a render probe, deliberately. The defect was
an ABSENCE, and a DOM probe cannot distinguish "silently dropped" from "the recommender
had nothing to suggest" -- which is exactly why this survived a green board and a passing
probe suite. tools/tests/test_nogoal_wanted_join.py replays the join over the shipped
layout data, asserts nothing is dropped when joining on `key`, then PLANTS the old
display-name join and asserts it still loses exactly those 16. It also pins the source
line, so reverting the fix reddens the test instead of passing quietly.

This changes what the app does: with no goals set, the Coverage rail will now recommend
products against vitamin gaps, which it has never done. Approved before making the
change, and flagged for a look on screen.

summary: Fixed four reported defects: the Daily Protocol delete X (an unscoped rule in the scanner stylesheet captured it), tile click-through (my own regression from the vitamin fix), silver rendering as 0 mg, and declared-zero products listed as sources.
detail:
Four defects the owner hit, one of them mine.

THE DELETE X. On the Coverage tab's Daily Protocol box, every item's remove button was
stacked on a single point at the panel's top-right, so the one X you could see deleted
whichever row happened to be on top. The cause was in a third file entirely:
workspace-scanner.css carried an unscoped rule for the shared row-remove class, and
because that sheet loads after the coverage sheet at identical specificity, it captured
the Coverage rail's buttons and absolutely-positioned all of them to the same spot.
Measured: all three at (1537,492), outside the panel. The Scanner does not even use that
class, and every neighbouring rule in that block is correctly scoped to .vd-rail -- that
one line had lost its prefix. That is why fixing this once before did not hold: nothing
was wrong in either file you would think to look at. A new test now forbids a workspace
sheet from declaring a bare rule for a class another workspace owns, with a negative
control that replants the exact rule and an over-fire control that must spare a properly
scoped one.

THE TILE CLICK. This one I broke earlier today and it is worth being plain about.
slugToTileKey() had three callers serving two different contracts -- the DOM matches on
the tile's display name, the coverage snapshot matches on the canonical key. Fixing the
vitamin recommender by repointing that one map silently broke the tile click-through, which
is the only entrance to an essential's detail page, and the goal hover with it, for exactly
the same 16 tiles. There are now two maps with the contract stated on each, and the test
pins both plus all three call sites.

THE 0 MG. Colloidal silver lists 0.04 mg and the sources row rounded it to "0 mg" -- the
app asserting a product contains none of the thing it was recommending it for. Sub-milligram
composition figures now render in mcg, which is the unit such a quantity is written in
everywhere else. Silver reads 40 mcg and 13 mcg. Separately, 16 candidates carry an amount
of exactly zero -- a label declaring "Sodium 0mg" -- and those are no longer listed as
sources at all, because a product that declares none of a nutrient is not a source of it.

NOT REPRODUCED, AND SAID SO. The owner also reports that amino acids and fatty acids never
cover on a non-default regimen slot. A fresh profile shows 11 of 12 amino acids covered on
BOTH the default slot and a second one, whether the slot is created programmatically or by
clicking the empty slot tile, using the product he named. The mechanism I most suspected -- a
non-slot-scoped legacy storage key -- is dead: the coverage math reads none. Rather than
guess, his exported backup is needed so the real slot document can be loaded and the
difference found.

summary: Dose steppers no longer scroll the page to the top, and flavonoids posts Wallach's 1,000 mg lower bound instead of the unreachable 5,000. The signed-off header golden is left red pending the owner's call.
detail:
Two changes the owner asked for, plus one red I deliberately left standing.

THE DOSE BUTTONS. Stepping a dose up or down repainted the whole workspace, and because
both Coverage and Regimen repaint by replacing their container's innerHTML, the shared
scroller snapped back to the top every time. On a 91-tile field that meant finding your
place again after every single click. The fix captures the scroll position, paints, and
restores it in the same frame -- deliberately not on an animation frame, because that
would paint the top of the page once first, which is the flash itself. Measured at 500
and 348 pixels down; both held. The new probe carries a negative control asserting the
page really was scrolled first, because otherwise a page too short to scroll would pass
it while proving nothing. One honest limit: this stops the jump, not the repaint. Regimen
still rebuilds its whole subtree, so a faint flash can remain.

FLAVONOIDS. The board was asking for 5,000 mg. The best flavonoid source in the entire
catalog carries 100 mg, and all four stacked reach 143 mg -- under 3% -- so that tile
could never have left "gap" no matter what anyone bought. It now posts 1,000 mg.

Worth being precise about what that is and is not. It is NOT a source-rule exception:
1,000 is Wallach's own lower bound, printed in the same sentence of the same sealed claim
as the 5,000. Both ends are his. What bent is the project's own derive policy of always
posting the upper end of a stated range, and that bend is now a single named entry in the
generator with its reasoning written beside it.

The gate was taught rather than bypassed. amounts_wallach_only will accept a lower-end
posting only if it equals that claim's lower bound exactly and declares itself with a
reason; it goes red on a value that is neither end, on a missing reason, on a reason
written as prose, and on a provenance that declares both ends at once. Five negative
controls cover those. The first attempt also tripped prose_contained, which was right --
the explanation does not belong in shipped fact data, so the artifact carries a short
token and the prose stays in the generator.

THE RED I LEFT. render_probe_mech_shape byte-compares four signed-off element headers
against a stored golden, and today's display fixes legitimately changed them: zinc's
source row now reads 700 mcg where the golden holds 0.7 mg, and copper and vitamin A lost
source rows because products declaring zero of a nutrient are no longer listed as sources
of it. The mcg change is what he asked for. The zero-row change was my own inference. That
golden exists to pin design he has approved, so re-capturing it is his decision and I have
not made it for him.

summary: Five diet-routed nutrients now explain where Wallach says they come from, grounded in his own words and correcting the example lists. Golden re-captured; it exposed an 82% overstatement on zinc. Taurine and the vehicle crediting were not implemented.
detail:
Five nutrients - chloride, sulfur, flavonoids, vitamin K and potassium - now carry a
short note on their detail page saying where Wallach says they actually come from. Without it,
someone reading chloride's 2,500 mg target against a best product of 72 mg concludes the app is
broken, when the honest answer is that he names salt as the source.

The research corrected the owner's own examples rather than echoing them, which is what he asked
for. Wallach names organ meats for sulfur - not eggs or turkey. For potassium he names grains,
fruits and vegetables as categories and no individual food anywhere in seven books - no banana,
no spinach. Flavonoids are cocoa, tea, wine, dark chocolate and dark fruits and berries; parsley
and oregano appear nowhere.

One framing point mattered more than the food lists. He asked for notes saying these come from
food rather than from supplements, and the corpus contradicts that: all five keep their own line
in his Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program. So each note says the diet does most of the work
without claiming he thinks supplementation is unnecessary, because the second claim would put
words in his mouth.

The gate caught the first attempt. prose_contained refused prose in a fact field, which was
right; sourcesNote is now a registered prose home beside lede and why - refined rather than
exempted.

The signed-off header golden was re-captured with approval, and the diff was read line by line
before it was accepted. It held only the two intended changes, and it surfaced a defect nobody
had reported: zinc's Ultimate Iodine row is 0.055 mg, which the old formatter rendered as
"0.1 mg" - an 82% overstatement. It now reads 55 mcg. Selenium came back byte-identical, the
control proving the re-capture touched only what it should have.

Three research findings are recorded in the contradictions file, one of them a correction to my
own earlier writing in that same file. I had proposed deriving per-element amounts from the
plant-derived assay via ppm times 600 mg of solids. That formula is wrong by a factor of 49.3.
The table is real - printed twice, in Epigenetics and as Rare Earths Table 10-5, byte-identical
between the two, fully legible - so the belief that it was undisclosed was mistaken. But its
basis is per litre of liquid, not per kilogram of solids, and six of its elements are given as
grams per litre, which is not a parts-per-million figure at all. That per-litre reading is an
inference from internal consistency rather than a sentence Wallach wrote, and it is recorded as
an inference.

Silver, germanium and silica came back presence-only with active counter-evidence: he lists
colloidal silver and the plant-derived vehicle side by side as separate items, he doses germanium
separately inside the very list that names the vehicle, and silica's stated sources are
high-fibre diets and beer. Tin remains the only element with vehicle-supply language.

Taurine was not implemented. Wallach states no daily amount for it, and the proposed 200 mg
threshold traces to a Youngevity label, which is composition and can never drive a target.

summary: Taurine already works - measured, not inferred - so the proposed 200 mg threshold was unnecessary and would have been more restrictive. Germanium has no product data at all. Silica note added.
detail:
Three findings, two of which correct me.

TAURINE NEEDED NOTHING. It is already covered the moment any source carrying it is in the
regimen - no amount threshold at all. Two products carry a taurine row: Rebound FX at 200 mg
and Ultimate Cardio STX at 120 mg. Driving the real app proved it: adding Rebound FX moves
amino acids from 0 of 12 to 1 of 12 and the taurine tile turns covered. The proposed 200 mg
rule would have been more restrictive than what already ships, because it would have excluded
the 120 mg product.

I got there after three wrong turns worth recording. I queried the product file at the top
level and announced that no product lists taurine - the nutrient rows live one level down,
under components. I then mis-parsed the resolver artifact and announced taurine was missing
from it - it is there. Both mistakes were reasoning about data instead of driving the app,
and one headless run settled what three rounds of inference had got wrong.

GERMANIUM HAS NO PRODUCT DATA AT ALL - zero occurrences in the entire product pillar. Silver
appears on exactly two products, both standalone colloidal silvers. The owner reports that
both are listed as ingredients on the Youngevity pages for the liquid plant-derived products;
our records for those carry only an aggregate "Plant Derived Minerals" row. If the labels do
list them, that is a composition gap rather than a doctrine question, because Youngevity
composition is an allowed source. But the product pillar is sealed and only he can write it,
so it waits on his label data rather than on my inference.

THE SILICA NOTE says plainly that no Youngevity product supplies a meaningful amount. The one
food Wallach names is beer, which sits against his own insistence on avoiding barley. The note
leaves that tension as his rather than tidying it away, and leaves out the brown rice the
owner suggested - that is his inference, not Wallach's sentence, and the source rule binds him
too.

summary: Diet notes now span the full drawer width. Session handed off with the 90/90 composition gap as the active task: the products pillar carries no silver, germanium or tin for the liquid plant-derived products.
detail:
The notes added earlier carried a 66-character width cap that the owner flagged as
arbitrary next to the other drawer notes. Removed. Measured afterwards: the note now
renders at 817 pixels, exactly the width of the product rows and the section label above it.

The session closes with one clear active task, and it is not the doctrine argument I had
been having. He is right that all ninety cannot be covered, and the cause is measurable:
the product database simply does not record silver, germanium or tin for the liquid
plant-derived products. Germanium and tin appear nowhere in the entire file. Silver appears
only on two standalone colloidal silver products. Ultimate Classic carries thirty-three
nutrient rows and none of them is any of the three -- only a single aggregate plant-derived
minerals row.

He says the Youngevity product pages list silver and germanium as ingredients in those
formulas, and product composition is an allowed source under the source rule. So this is a
gap in our records rather than a question about what Wallach believes, and it closes with
his label figures followed by a seal, which is his act and never carries forward from a
past session.

summary: Six diet notes now name real food sources; the scanner can add a nutrient row it could not read; tin is covered by plant-derived minerals on Wallach's own words, and silver's 400 mcg turned out to be a limit he says you can take, not an amount he says you need.
detail:
Two of the ninety essentials were being judged against the wrong idea of what Wallach actually said, and the app now says the right thing about both.

TIN. Wallach never names a single food that contains tin -- not once across all seven books. What he does say, in two books sixteen years apart, is to get it "from plant derived colloidal minerals", and in a third place he mentions regrowing a good deal of his own hair using exactly that. So a bottle of plant-derived minerals in your regimen now covers tin. This is not a rule being bent for convenience; it is finally doing what he wrote. Tin keeps its own 500 mcg figure too, so if you add your own supplement that meets it, that still counts -- whichever route gets you there, the better answer wins.

SILVER. The board had been demanding 400 mcg of silver a day, which meant the best product in the catalogue looked like it needed ten servings to be enough. That felt absurd because it was. His actual sentence is "Humans can consume 400 mcg of silver per day" -- what you CAN take, not what you need. Silver has no row at all in his Base Line supplement table, the table every other figure of this kind comes from, and in his newest book he says outright that silver is not required by any known biological system. So the number stays on the page, labelled as the upper limit it is, and any product genuinely carrying silver now covers it.

THE DIET NOTES. The owner ruled that these notes exist to help a reader find real food, not to prove a citation, so they now name actual sources: eggs for sulfur, brown rice for silica, potatoes and beans and avocado for potassium, salt for sodium, garlic and shiitake and ginseng for germanium. The line I kept is that no food is ever put in Wallach's mouth -- where the text says "Wallach says", that is still him, and no note carries an amount or a health claim.

TWO THINGS I GOT WRONG ALONG THE WAY, BOTH CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING.

First, I nearly wrote "read a short product list here" for potassium and sodium. They carry 42 and 45 products. Running the actual app instead of reasoning about the data caught it.

Second, and worse: moving silver's number to a new field made the invariant board go green BECAUSE of the change. The gate that proves every amount traces to a Wallach book looks at a field called `low`; silver's figure moved to `ceiling`, so the gate simply stopped seeing it and reported all clear. A green board that is green for the wrong reason is the failure mode this project exists to prevent. The gate now audits a ceiling exactly the same way, with four new tests that deliberately poison it and confirm it turns red.

There was also a moment where fixing the lie created the opposite lie: with no target number, silver's page fell through to "Wallach never states an exact number for this one" -- which is false, he states 400 mcg. Deleting his number would have been its own dishonesty. It is shown, under its own heading.

GERMANIUM needed a structural fix to say anything at all. No Youngevity product contains germanium, and the "where this comes from" block was written to disappear entirely when no product carried the nutrient -- so the one essential most in need of "here is where you actually get this" was the only one that could never show it.

THE SCANNER can now add a row. Before, if you photographed a label the reader could not make out, you landed on a confirmation screen with nothing on it and no way forward. You can now type the rows in by hand, which is the only route into the app for a food, or for a bottle whose label the reader misses.

summary: The Codex is a real website now — nutrientcodex.com is live, behaves identically to the download, and opens in about a quarter of the data. Two hosting settings were wrong at launch; one would have frozen every visitor on today's build for six months.
detail:
He bought a domain and the Codex is now reachable on the web as well as by download. It
behaves exactly like the version you download — same board, same numbers, same knowledge — but it
starts up in roughly a quarter of the data it would have taken this morning. The downloadable
version has not changed at all and is still the main thing; the website is a second door into the
same room. Two settings on his hosting were wrong when it first went up. One of them would have
quietly locked every visitor onto today's version of the site for six months, so that nothing he
changed afterwards would ever have reached them. Both are fixed.

DOMAIN — nutrientcodex.com, his ruling, chosen from a shortlist verified available via RDAP
(Verisign for .com) with controls run FIRST: GOOGLE.COM -> 200 and a nonsense string -> 404, so the
instrument was shown to distinguish the two states before any candidate was trusted; finalists
cross-checked for absent NS records. Wallach's name is deliberately off it. His two reasons: he may
object one day, and it implies he built this. The load-bearing third: this app already contradicts
him on his own terms — silver's 400 mcg ruled a ceiling, tin ruled vehicle-supplied — and a name
that reads as HIS makes every such correction look like a betrayal instead of scholarship.
★ The entire "90" family was rejected DESPITE being available: 90minerals.com serves a live
Youngevity products site and 90essentials.com is a distributor with a sales phone number, so
branding on the framework's own number would have leaked type-in traffic to MLM sellers and made
the Codex look like the one thing it is not — a Youngevity storefront. Full shortlist and reasoning:
chronicle/decisions/2026-08-20-domain-name.md.

CHARTER — HIS RULING. CLAUDE.md's "no network at runtime / cannot be taken offline" now scopes to
the LOCAL build ONLY, which he considers already achieved and finished. The web build is a second
distribution and MAY fetch. Its goals, in his words: identical to local or better, as fast as
possible, and set-and-forget with minimal maintenance. He explicitly did NOT want a service worker
— there is no web-offline requirement, and a stale service-worker cache is the direct enemy of
set-and-forget.

WHAT WAS BUILT. tools/build_web.py packages dist-web/ (gitignored, never committed): minified
bundle, all 13 fonts TTF->WOFF2 (11.09 MB -> 5.54 MB, -50.1%), drops assets/data/ (13 MB, inlined at
build — verified nothing fetches it at runtime), worker-offline.js (17.2 MB, file://-only per
state/ocr.ts's existing protocol branch) and *.map (18.1 MB), content-hashes JS + CSS so a year-long
cache has no invalidation to ever think about, and emits .htaccess. It never touches source: every
transform runs on copies, which is also required because the design-system stylesheet is sealed.
Deploy 93 MB -> 38.6 MB. tools/esbuild_web.mjs is the web bundle, differing from the file build in
exactly two ways — --define:__SPLIT_DATA__=true, and an onLoad hook stubbing each SPLIT_ARTIFACT to
its schema-valid empty shape. It asserts on esbuild's own METAFILE that each stub actually applied,
because a silently re-inlined payload's only symptom would be a mysteriously large bundle.
state/data-split.ts fetches the split artifacts and is dormant in the file build. Hydrators were
added to state/log.ts, state/corpus.ts and state/search.ts, each clearing its parse cache so a
fetched payload re-validates through the same Zod boundary as an inlined one and earns no more
trust for having arrived over the wire.

★ ANTI-FAKERY CATCH. The rail renders a count DERIVED from the corpus. Before hydration
claimCount() returns 0, so the naive split would have printed "Corpus · 0 entries" — a number the
app does not have. It now shows the bare label until the count is knowable and repaints on a new
'corpus:hydrated' event; corpus.ts::isLoaded() derives that from the data itself rather than a
tracked flag, so there is no second piece of state to drift out of step with the first.

NEW GATE, shipped in the same patch as the comment that promised it (00.B.2).
split_data_manifest_agrees ties the three places that must agree: SPLIT_ARTIFACTS in
esbuild_web.mjs, the SplitKey union in data-split.ts, and the artifact's presence on disk. This
defect class is INVISIBLE LOCALLY — on file:// the artifact is still inlined, so a broken split
renders perfectly on this machine and empties only on the website. Negative test
tools/tests/test_split_data_manifest.py reds on all five drift shapes, including a vacuous pass on
an empty manifest. ★ Its first version hardcoded the one-key union text and broke the moment the
list grew to three. It failed LOUDLY rather than passing vacuously, which was correct — but a
fixture that breaks every time the list it guards changes is a fixture that eventually gets deleted
rather than fixed, so it now derives its tampering from whatever the real files currently say.

MEASURED. First load over the wire 3.95 MB -> 0.96 MB locally, 0.92 MB live (SiteGround serves
brotli, beating the gzip estimate). Bundle 3.16 MB -> 402 KB gzipped. The three split artifacts:
search-index 987 KB, creators-log 958 KB — a development log that was in every user's first paint —
and corpus-embed 726 KB.

★★ LIVE-HOST FINDING, the one worth remembering. SiteGround fronts Apache with NGINX and serves
static files DIRECTLY by default, which bypasses .htaccess entirely. Proven, not guessed:
Server: nginx, and neither X-Content-Type-Options nor Referrer-Policy — set ONLY in our file —
appeared on any response. Two consequences. The .gz protection was working by NGINX's
octet-stream default rather than by our ForceType, i.e. correct by luck. And index.html came back
Cache-Control: max-age=15552000 — 180 days — which pins a returning visitor to one build for six
months and would have made every future update invisible to them, defeating the content-hashing
outright. Fixed at Site Tools -> Speed -> Caching -> NGINX Direct Delivery OFF. HTTPS Enforce was
also off (http:// served 200 rather than redirecting) and is now on. Recorded above the .htaccess
template in tools/build_web.py with the one-line curl that proves whether the rules are live at all.

★ MEASUREMENT CORRECTION MID-SWEEP. My first pass reported the JSON artifacts arriving
uncompressed. That was my instrument, not his server: curl -I sends no Accept-Encoding, so the
server correctly did not compress. Re-measured with the header set, everything arrives brotli. The
correction was reported instead of the false alarm.

ALSO FOUND BY MEASURING. 10.24 MB of fonts ship but are NEVER fetched — Merriweather x2 = 9.16 MB,
Playfair x2, Crimson x2 — because type-futurist.css remaps the serif and display tokens to Space
Grotesk and Unbounded. Confirmed twice: by network trace, and by --ds-font-serif resolving to
'Space Grotesk'. NOT removed — that needs a theme audit first and the sheet is sealed. Converting
them to WOFF2 takes half the win at zero risk.

MY ERROR, RECOVERED. I called safe_write.safe_rewrite(path, payload_file_path). The module function
takes the payload STRING, not a path, so it wrote a 148-byte path into main.ts and reported OK —
its intent-check compares the landed bytes to the payload, and they matched perfectly, because the
payload really was that string. Restored via git checkout HEAD and reapplied from the staged
content; nothing was lost. Written up in the tooling-traps memory.

VERIFIED. node tools/build.mjs -> Build OK (exit 0). invariants.py -> 95/95 passed (0 failed),
external still 23/23. 45/45 control tests. Dashboard typecheck clean. vitest 50/50. Render probes
37/39 — the only two failures are the documented stale group_dots + orac, red before this session,
failing for their documented reasons with 0 page errors. ★ A/B DRIVEN IN A REAL BROWSER across
local, packaged and live: 579 DOM nodes / 492 coverage tiles / visible-text hash 3873002722 on all
three; Corpus · 2,611 entries, matching the 2,611 claims in the source embed exactly; Creator's Log
911 entries, matching the source artifact exactly; Knowledge drawer 166 nodes. The local build
reports dataFetches: [] — it still fetches nothing, from anywhere. Negative controls on the payloads
actually leaving the web bundle: 'round-close' 272 -> 2 occurrences, 'knowledge_version' 68 -> 1.
Live OCR model: 200, no Content-Encoding, gzip magic 1f 8b 08 08 intact, all 12,821,300 bytes.
0 console errors, 0 failed resources. CLAUDE.md gate count 94 -> 95, caught by the board's own
meta-gate.

NOT DONE, STATED PLAINLY. The visual pass is NOT done: the Browser pane would not composite frames
all session, so every claim above is structural rather than visual, and human eyes remain the gate.
The site does NOT yet tell a file:// user that localStorage is per-origin and their profile will not
appear on the website — a returning user currently sees an empty board and will conclude their data
is gone, which is the highest-value copy change outstanding. Mobile is entirely untested and is the
next session's task. The live site's Creator's Log will read 911 until the next deploy, because this
very entry lands in the ledger after the upload.

summary: Everyone now starts on the same five-product pack instead of a scorer that gave every goal the same answer, the dose counts tablets rather than servings, and the omega bars finally move when you change it.
detail:
The recommendation engine had a quiet failure: it gave nearly the same answer no matter which health goal you picked. Not a bug exactly — it was ranking correctly, but the question had the same answer for everyone, so 124 recommendation slots across every goal were filled by only twelve distinct products. The fix is two-part. A curated starting set of five products now opens the list in a fixed order, the same for everyone, so the opening is a deliberate choice rather than an accident of arithmetic. Behind it, each further recommendation is now chosen for what the ones above it did NOT cover, so the list spans your gaps instead of repeating itself.

The dose stepper also stopped lying by omission. It counted servings and printed a bare number, so a product whose serving is two tablets showed "1". The maths was right, but read "1" as one tablet, step it to two, and you have quietly asked for four. It now counts the product's own units and says so — "2 tablets/day". Nobody's coverage number moved: the same amount is delivered, it is just finally labelled.

And the omega bars now fill as you raise an oil's dose, instead of sitting empty and then snapping full.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

GOAL MERGE. `fewer-colds-flu` retired into `stronger-immunity` (31 -> 30 goals). All four conditions absorbed, because `colds` is the ONLY carrier of potassium — via WAL-CLM-LETS-000225 — and dropping it as a near-duplicate of `common_cold` would have deleted potassium from the merged goal with no gate going red. Members re-derived: 15 -> 16, potassium present. Three MEASURED comment figures were re-measured rather than edited by eye; the all-five-dots probability moved 9% -> 11%, the product-breadth counts did not move at all. Fixed a latent defect while there: views/welcome.ts never resolved saved goal ids against the layout, so a retired id would render no chip, could never be deselected, and would hold one of five goal slots forever.

THE STARTER PACK. New curated starter-pack.json (kids-exclusion pattern, fail-loud). Root cause of the sameness, measured not argued: `goalIds` is computed in the ranker and never enters the score, and the breadth term reads each product's GLOBAL breadth — so it cannot vary by goal. Greedy gap-fill is OPT-IN; the non-greedy path is the original one-shot code byte-preserved, because the condition pages ask a different question and both relative terms rescale with the surviving set.

CAPS. Coverage: three at a time, no pager — the list ADVANCES, since an added product leaves it and the next surfaces. Capped by a budget of nine minus the Youngevity products already in the regimen; driven end to end, owned 0->9 offered 9->0. Nothing persisted; `owned` is derived every paint.

SUPERSEDED PRODUCTS. Four of six BTT/Tangy Tangerine products retired against BTT 2.5. Found by DRIVING the app rather than by grep: BTT Original was offered beside BTT 2.5 in a real session. Kept as a separate curation from kids-exclusion, whose gate and docs are specifically about children's formulations.

THE EFA BARS. fillPercent had a branch only for the plant-derived aggregate; everything else fell through to a ratio that needs a numeric target and otherwise returns a binary 0/1. So the omega tiles snapped empty-to-full. Now mirrors the PDM branch. 33/44/56/67% at doses 3-6.

DOSE IN UNITS. serving_units/serving_unit derived from each label's own serving_size, single-component countable products only (98 of 98 solid components parse; 91 of 215 qualify; the five multi-component ones get none because no single count is true for them). Stored amounts stay per-serving and readScale still returns servings — only the displayed count and step size changed.

★ HIS PREMISE WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED WITH EVIDENCE RATHER THAN IMPLEMENTED. He asked for the default to become 2 because the amounts were "per unit". They are not: Ultimate Daily's vitamin A is stored as 1,200 mcg with pct_dv 133, and 1200/900 = 133%, so 1,200 mcg IS the two-tablet amount. 96% of nutrient rows corroborate per-serving once BOTH FDA Daily-Value eras are allowed — the apparent mismatches were pre-2016 label columns, not a per-unit split. Implementing his request literally would have computed four tablets a day. Likewise "Ultimate Daily adds 2" was the greedy delta, not a dose artifact: Ultimate Classic already covers 22 of its 24 essentials, and the only two it brings are iodine and methionine.

§00.A. Ultimate EFA Plus defaulting to 3/day was RAISED as the one number from neither the product label nor a Wallach book — container arithmetic, 90 softgels over 30 days — and RATIFIED by him against 9/day (which IS Wallach's 9,000 mg EFA figure) and 1/day (the bare label serving). Recorded with provenance `container_life`. The tiles still grade against the corpus target, so the shortfall shows as a third-full bar rather than being hidden.

THREE NEW GATES, 95 -> 98, each shipped in the same patch as the thing it governs. starter_pack_resolves was NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED — all seven planted defects go red. superseded_products_not_recommended asserts both halves of the asymmetry. dose_defaults_are_not_wallach keeps a curated starting quantity from ever acquiring Wallach's authority: the provenance vocabulary is closed and has no wallach member, and no entry may carry a claim id.

THE GATES CAUGHT TWO REAL BUGS OF MINE. dose_defaults_are_not_wallach found that the Regimen add path matches the vault by NAME and so never applied the curated quantities at all. no_new_dead_code found two speculative exports, deleted rather than baselined. And no_product_marketing_prose went red on the two new vault keys — refined, not widened: the keys are admitted WITH their values pinned, because a bare allowlist entry would have left a free string in the one gate whose whole job is keeping prose out.

A PROBE ASSERTION WAS WRONG, NOT MY CHANGE. `s2.gap < s1.gap` after a dose step was never the law — it only ever passed by accident of which product ranked first. A dose increase can only move essentials the product CONTAINS, and those sit in PARTIAL. Measured: covered 12 -> 49, partial 49 -> 12, gap 14 -> 14. Now asserts (partial + gap) falls.

RAIL POLISH — and the screenshot lied twice. `grid-row: 1 / -1` cannot reach implicit rows without grid-template-rows, so the span silently collapsed to row 1 and centred the close button on the NAME line, 11px high. Fixing that to `span 2` still measured -11, because the full-width footer could then find no free row and auto-placed into a THIRD one. Only computed styles caught either. Pinning the footer to an explicit cell is what actually centred it.

REGIMEN PANEL. The gauge — not the category cluster beside it — was what set the panel's height, so it was the only cut that bought real space: 252 -> 200px, numeral scaled with it. The readout's grid gap was deliberately NOT reduced; the squares are aspect-ratio 1 in a 45-column grid, so a smaller gap makes each square wider and the block taller. Measured, not assumed. "Best next moves" climbed from ~860 to 764 and the first card now sits fully inside a 900px fold.

NO SEALED PILLAR WAS TOUCHED, so no seal ceremony was required or performed.

BLOCKED: the foods recommendation system on both tabs sits at turn 1 of the three-turn source-rule protocol. He chose to admit an outside food-composition table, which the closed allowlist does not permit; turn 2 must be a later turn. The repo holds ZERO per-food nutrient composition, all 77 sealed food_source claims carry a null dose, and a direct probe of all seven book texts (~5.7M chars) found approximately ONE food-to-amount datapoint. That is a data problem no mining campaign can close.
